metadata.title: Imagines Coronatae — crowned sacred images attested in the official acts of the Holy See
metadata.source: Acta Sanctae Sedis (1865-1908) and Acta Apostolicae Sedis (1909- ), Libreria Editrice Vaticana
metadata.layer: attestations — one record per ACT that attests a crowning; see imagines-coronatae.json for one record per IMAGE
metadata.method: Every ASS and AAS volume PDF published on vatican.va was downloaded and verified against its Content-Length, its text layer extracted, de-hyphenated across line breaks, and swept for the Latin and vernacular vocabulary of image-coronation. Candidate passages were read and structured by parallel extraction agents against a fixed specification, then merged and de-duplicated by locality.

evidence_types.papal_coronation_act: The act itself grants or permits the coronation.
evidence_types.papal_legate_deputation: The Pope deputes a Legate to crown the image in his name.
evidence_types.papal_personal_coronation: The act records that the Pope crowned the image himself.
evidence_types.retrospective_attestation: Another act (e.g. a Basilica Minor elevation) states in passing that the image was crowned.
evidence_types.norms: General legislation on the crowning of images.

caveats: NOT A GLOBAL CENSUS. For most of the period covered, the crowning of an image was decreed by the Chapter of St Peter’s Basilica (Capitulum Vaticanum) and was never published in either gazette. This dataset documents what ASS and AAS attest — a well-defined and citable subset.

The archives of the Chapter of St Peter’s Basilica are a separate source and only fractionally online. The dedicated series is “Madonne coronate” (cited BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo I, foglio N (mecc. N)); one volume is digitized in full, Arch.Cap.S.Pietro.Madonne.coron.4 (726 images, not OCR’d), and ten folios of vol. 19. Everything else must be consulted at the Vatican Library or the Archivio Capitolare, or reached through the registers and catalogues that cite it. See docs/CHAPTER-ARCHIVES.md.
The 25 March 1973 Normae (AAS 65, 276) reshaped the practice; from 1974 the acts appear as Litterae Apostolicae granting the faculty to crown, and they are numerous.

Sources are OCR scans and ASS is markedly rougher than AAS. Place names are frequently mangled. Every record keeps the verbatim Latin rubric and incipit and carries a confidence value; records marked "low", or carrying a note, should be checked against the printed page before being treated as authoritative.
Several ASS volumes span two calendar years; `year` is the first year of the volume.
metadata.license: Underlying ASS and AAS texts are © Libreria Editrice Vaticana. This compilation is provided for research use.
metadata.structure: One record per CROWNED IMAGE. Every ASS/AAS act that attests it is kept in that image’s `sources` array, so an image cited in several volumes is ONE record with several sources, not several records. Images are identified by locality first, since Marian titles repeat worldwide; a distinctive title can also unite an image crowned away from its shrine.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.rubric_latin: Beata Maria Virgo « Afrorum Domina » praecipua Patrona totius archidioecesis Algeriensis declaratur.
sources.incipit_latin: Praefervidum erga intaminatam Dei Genetricem amorem etiam in repositis terris inter omnes constat vigere. Iam inde antiquitus in regione Algeriensi
sources.notes: Patron declaration stating 'Anno MDCCCLXXVI Decessor Noster ven. mem. Pius Pp. IX ecclesiam ... ad Basilicae Minoris honorem et dignitatem evexit, et statuam Beatae Mariae Virginis aurea corona, suo nomine et auctoritate, redimiri iussit'. OCR renders the year as 'm d c c c l x x v ï' = MDCCCLXXVI (1876). The bronze statue was given by the Children of Mary of Lyons and blessed by the first bishop of Algiers in 1840 ('anno MDCCCXXXX'). Pius XII/John XXIII text also records that John XXIII himself visited the shrine on 19 March 1950.

sources.act_type: Epistola
sources.rubric_latin: AD R. P. D. BARNABAM PIEDRABUENA, EPISCOPUM CATAMARCENSIUM, DE SOLLEMNIBUS GRATULATUR, QUAE B. M. V. « DEL VALLE » APPARANTUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Litteris tuis officio functus es grato admodum Nobis. Nuntiasti enim Catamarcensium catholicorum in almam Dei Matrem adeo studia exardescere
sources.notes: The batch passage is the volume index (printed p. 500), whose entry ('Litteris tuis. - Ad R. P. D. Barnabam Piedrabuena, episcopum Catamarciensium, de sollemnibus gratulatur, quae B. M. V. « dei Valle » apparantur') does not itself mention a crowning; the crowning is attested in the act it points to, read in txt/AAS-08-1916-ocr.txt at printed p. 144: 'iidem, labente vicesimo quinto anno ex quo Virginis simulacrum, sollemni Ecclesiae ritu, aureo donatum est diademate, velint huius eventus faustitatem iteranda pietatis significatione commemorare'. `page` therefore set to 144, not to the index page 500. coronation_date 1891 is arithmetic: the 25th year was running in 1916 ('labente vicesimo quinto anno'); the act itself states no year, so verify. The act names no authority for the original coronation beyond 'sollemni Ecclesiae ritu'. Country inferred from the see of Catamarca (the act speaks of an Apostolic Legate 'apud istam Rempublicam'). The Legate named in the act (Achilles, titular archbishop of Thessalonica) is deputed for the 1916 anniversary solemnities, not for the coronation, so `legate` is left null.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.rubric_latin: ECCLESIA CATHEDRALIS CAIAMARCENSIS, TITULO B. MARIAE VIRG. «A VALLE», BASILICAE MINORIS PRIVILEGIIS HONORIBUSQUE AUGETUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Postulat a Nobis Venerabilis Frater Catamarcensium Episcopus, intra fines Reipublicae Argentinae, quinquagesimi anni occasione ab imposita corona aurea, qua statua Beatae Mariae Virginis a Valle ... redimita fuit
sources.notes: Basilica Minor grant made on the fiftieth anniversary of the crowning: 'quinquagesimi anni occasione ab imposita corona aurea, qua statua Beatae Mariae Virginis a Valle, in templo Cathedrali suo servata, redimita fuit'. coronation_date 1891 is computed from that fifty-year interval (act dated 1941), not stated explicitly - please verify. Rubric OCR 'CAIAMARCENSIS' for 'CATAMARCENSIS'; the body reads 'Catamarcensium Episcopus'. Datum reads 'die u m. Iulii' (= II, 2 July). No act numeral: the section heading is a bare 'LITTERAE APOSTOLICAE'.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.rubric_latin: Sanctuario Dominae Nostrae del Valle Catamarcensis dioecesis Rosa aurea tribuitur.
sources.incipit_latin: Ab incohato iam saeculo XVII Beatam Mariam Virginem del Valle colere coeperunt fideles, cuius signum Decessor Noster Leo XIII, insignis memoriae, coronavit.
sources.notes: Golden Rose grant ('Ad futuram rei memoriam') which attests in passing that Leo XIII crowned the image. No coronation year is given in the act — left null rather than supplied. Country not stated; inferred from the diocese of Catamarca (Argentina). The Golden Rose was to be presented by Card. Franciscus Xaverius Errázuriz Ossa.

Their note: Statua del XVI secolo del tipo "conochia" di fattura spagnola. sources.act_type: Epistola
sources.legate: Iosephus Ernestus Card. Van Roey, Archiepiscopus Mechliniensis
sources.rubric_latin: AD EM.UM P. D. IOSEPHUM ERNESTUM TIT. S. MARIAE DE ARACOELI S. R. E. PRESB. CARDINALEM VAN ROEY, ARCHIEPISCOPUM MECHLINIENSEM, QUEM LEGATUM SUUM MITTIT AD SOLEMNIA QUINQUIES SAECULARIA UNIVERSITATIS STUDIORUM LOVANIENSIS CELEBRANDA.
sources.incipit_latin: Quinto feliciter exeunte saeculo ex quo Lovaniensis ista Studiorum Universitas condita est, iuste quidem Rector eius magnificus Paulinus Ladeuze
sources.notes: Act I begins on printed p. 307 (verified in txt/AAS-19-1927-ocr.txt); rubric and incipit taken from there; the coronation reference is on the passage page 308: 'auspice Virgine Matre, quam ab ipso iam initio veluti Sedem Sapientiae venerari consueverunt Lovanienses, cuiusque augusta effigies, Nostro quidem nomine, corona aurea mox redimietur'. The legation is primarily for the university's fifth-centenary solemnities; the crowning is to be done in the Pope's name ('Nostro nomine'), presumably by the same Legate, but the letter does not say so expressly. Coronation year 1927 inferred from 'mox' and the date of the act. Diocese given as that of the Legate's see (Louvain lay in the archdiocese of Mechelen); country inferred.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.rubric_latin: BASILICAE MINORIS HONORIBUS DECORATUR TEMPLUM-SANCTUARIUM BEATAE MARIAE VIRGINIS DE « COPACABANA », INTRA FINES DIOECESIS PACENSIS IN BOLIVIA.

sources.notes: Coronation mentioned only in passing and without date or agent: 'Deiparae Virginis statua in eodem honorifice servatur, quam recentiori tempore sollemniter etiam aureo diademate redimitam, boliviani christifideles peculiari cultu venerantur'. sources.act_type: Epistula

sources.incipit_latin: Celebranti feliciter tibi, quattuor abhinc annos, quinque ab inito episcopatu lustra, existimationem ac benevolentiam Nostram palam significavimus, praecipua tua erga Ecclesiam merita
sources.notes: Jubilee letter to Card. Gaetano Cicognani; the coronation is mentioned only retrospectively on printed p. 528: « In Bolivia autem, ubi Nuntius nominatus fuisti, dum saeculum celebrabatur, ex quo res publica in libertatem vindicata erat, Sanctae Sedis Legatum extraordinarium egisti et insigni Virginis simulacro de Copacabana ... auream coronam imposuisti ». The year is not stated; the act places it during the centenary of Bolivian independence (i.e. 1925) — left null rather than computed. Locality 'Copacabana' is taken from the image's title and the description of the lakeside sanctuary; vernacular title is a normalisation. Country is explicit ('In Bolivia').

sources.notes: Patronage act (patron of the Bolivian Navy); coronation attested in passing: 'iam Praedecessores Nostri Pius XI effigiem ipsam aureo diademate redimiri et Pius XII templum titulo ac dignitate Basilicae Minoris decorari censuerunt' - no year for the crowning. sources.notes: Legate letter for the Brazilian national Marian Congress at São Paulo; the Legate (Card. Piazza) is deputed to preside at the Congress, not to crown, so this is a retrospective attestation: 'simulque quinquaginta implentur anni, ex quo augustum simulacrum aurea corona redimitum est Nostrae Dominae « da Conceiçâo Aparecida », Brasiliae Patronae'. Coronation year 1904 computed from 'quinquaginta implentur anni' relative to the act year 1954; not stated verbatim. The shrine's own locality/diocese is not named — only that the cult had its cradle in the Archdiocese of São Paulo. OCR 'Conceiçâo' for 'Conceição'.

sources.notes: Televised message of Paul VI to Chile for the dedication of the national votive temple of Our Lady of Mount Carmel at Maipú. This is a papal DONATION of a crown, not a liturgical coronation rite, and the Pope was not present in person (message sent from Rome); classified papal_personal_coronation per the gap-spec rule for papal gifts of a crown, but a checker should verify whether a coronation ceremony followed. No coronation date is given. Act begins on printed page 727 (rubric there); the passage window is anchored at 729, where the crown sentence stands. sources.rubric_latin: Concessa Facultas Coronandi Sacras Imagines Jesù, et Beatæ Mariæ Virginis Existentes in Ecclesia F. F. C. C. Reformatorum S. Francisci Loci Tarsacti in Dalmatia
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'duas nempe Coronas aureas imponens, unam Iconi Beatissimae Virginis MARIAE, alteram JESU'. Petitioner: Fr. Petrus Francetich (Francievich) à Flumine, Guardian, and the whole Reformed Franciscan convent of Tersatto ('ad instantiam R.di Patris Petri Francetich Guardiani et totius Conventus') — the original petition to the Chapter is not in this range. Contents: silversmith's account of 18 June 1713 ('Iomaso Vanni e Comp.') for two gold crowns 'per la Madonna SS.ma e Suo Bambino nella Chiesa in una Città di Dalmatia', f. 205r (margin 'Nº 230', 'loco detto [Tersatto]'); letter of the bishop of Verona, Verona 3 Aug 1713, acknowledging receipt of the crowns via the bishop of Traù and the faculty to substitute another bishop (ff. 206r–v; OCR 'Teramo' = Tersatto); notarial instrument, Tersatto 14 Sept 1715 (second copy reads 24 Sept), notary Franciscus Laurentius Fracassa, embedding the Chapter's letter of Rome 17 June 1713 (secretary Giacinto Sacripante; second copy OCR '1717'), the Chapter's rite instructions, the subdelegation of Venice 14 Sept 1714 (notary Laurentius Rosetti/Bosetti, nuncio Alexander Aldobrandini) and of Brescia 24 July 1715, and the convent's obligation to keep the crowns (ff. 207r–209v), authenticated by the judges of Fiume 4 Oct 1715 (f. 210r); wrapper f. 211v ('Mons.r Vesc.o di Verona circa la coronazione della B. V. Bambino Giesù esistente nella chiesa de PP. Riformati di S. Fra. in Farsado 1713', margin 'N. 512'); printed 'Vera Effigie della Madre di Dio dipinta da S. Luca e mandata da Urbano V l'anno 1362 a Tersatto' (f. 212r — mentions indulgences of Pius VII and Leo XII, so a 19th-c. print inserted later); letter of the crowning bishop ('Il Ves.co De Menti' = de Marotti), Fiume 14/19 Sept 1715, stating he crowned 'a 8. del corrente' the miraculous image painted by St Luke (ff. 213r–214r). Also at f. 212v a heading 'Conto dell'Ill.mo e Rev.mo Capitolo di S. Pietro delle Corone d'oro — Pro informat.e 1706 7 Octobris — Gio. Giardini Argentiere', a general silversmith account naming no image (not emitted). Country: documents say 'in Dalmatia' and 'Provincie Austriache'; Tersatto/Fiume is modern Trsat/Rijeka, Croatia (inference from the unambiguous place). The wrapper f. 211v also names Leuca — see separate low-confidence record.

sources.act_type: Allocutio
sources.rubric_latin: Ad Cubae sacros praesules.
sources.incipit_latin: Me complace recibirlos en esta Audiencia, a pocos meses de mi recordado viaje a su Patria.
sources.notes: Allocution (in Spanish) to the bishops of Cuba on their ad limina visit, AAS 91 (1999) 105-109, dated 'Die 9 Iunii 1998'; the coronation reference stands on printed page 109, at the end of the act (printed_page of the passage is 109, but the act begins on 105). The Pope names only the devotional title, with no word for image: 'A la Virgen de la Caridad del Cobre, Madre de todos los cubanos, recordando con emocion el momento en que le ceni la corona que sus hijos le ofrecieron...' - i.e. he himself set on her the crown her children had offered. The crowning took place during his apostolic visit to Cuba (the act refers to 'mi visita a Cuba' / 'mi inolvidable Viaje' of January 1998, citing his 21 January 1998 Havana airport address, so coronation_date is given as 1998); the exact day and place (Santiago de Cuba, 24 January 1998) are NOT stated in the source and have not been supplied. Country 'Cuba' is explicit in the text ('Madre de todos los cubanos', address to the Cuban bishops). No sanctuary or diocese is named.

sources.act_type: Homilia (Iter Apostolicum in Mexicum)
sources.rubric_latin: Nulla deinceps intermissa mora, Missam una cum omnibus Reipublicae Dominicanae Episcopis celebravit in Platea, quae ab Independentia nuncupatur, fidelium populo refertissima; postque lectum Evangelium hanc Summus Pontifex homiliam habuit
sources.notes: THE RECORD THIS GAP PASS EXISTS FOR. Homily of John Paul II at the Mass in the Plaza de la Independencia, Santo Domingo, 25 January 1979, first stop of the Iter Apostolicum in Mexicum (AAS 71, 149 ff.; the day is headed 'Die 25 m. Ianuarii', p. 150). Spanish sentence, verbatim: 'Amad a Cristo, amad al hombre por El y vivid la devoción a nuestra querida Madre del cielo, a quien invocáis con el hermoso nombre de Nuestra Señora de la Altagracia, a la que el Papa quiere dejar como homenaje de devoción una diadema.' No word for image appears anywhere near it — the devotion is named by its title only, which is why the mechanical filter dropped it. What the source states is that the Pope wishes to LEAVE a diadem as a homage of devotion; it is not described as a formal liturgical coronation. The homily begins on printed page 155 ('postque lectum Evangelium hanc Summus Pontifex homiliam habuit'); page set to 158, where the diadem sentence stands, as cited by the coordinator. AAS does not name the sanctuary of Higüey; earlier the same day, in the cathedral of Santo Domingo, the Pope prayed 'por intercesión de Nuestra Señora de la Altagracia, cuya imagen está aquí presente' (p. 155) — the only mention of an image. Locality 'Santo Domingo' is the place of the homily, not necessarily the home of the image. Body is in Spanish, so no Latin incipit; rubric_latin is the Latin editorial narrative introducing the homily on p. 155.

sources.incipit_latin: Vetustis sacris aedibus Deo in honorem Deiparae Virginis dicatis, ac splendidiorem ipsius cultum in Gallia efferentibus, merito accensenda est
sources.notes: Retrospective mention inside a minor-basilica elevation: "Pervetustum ipsius Virginis Dei Genitricis simulacrum, prodigiis clarum, aureoque diademate Summi Pontificis nomine anno 1865 redimitum" - i.e. crowned with a golden diadem in the name of the Supreme Pontiff in 1865. Place given by OCR as "Briconii"; identified as Saint-Brieuc because the petitioner is "Petrus Maria Fallieres Episcopus Briocensis et Trecorensis" - hence confidence medium rather than high. Other OCR damage on that page: "condecoran" for "condecorari", "supplicia ... vota" for "supplicia"/"supplicia vota". The coronation sentence stands on printed p. 400, just above the assigned passage window (the passage, printed_page 402, contains the end of this act); page recorded as 400 where the act and the coronation notice begin. Act dated 20 December 1902 (pontificate year 25) though printed in vol. 36 (1903-04).

sources.act_type: Epistola
sources.rubric_latin: AD R. P. D. FRANCISCUM M. GIEURE, BAIONENSIUM EPISCOPUM, OCCASIONE CORONATIONE B. MARIAE V. « DU BEAU RAMEAU », AD TEMPLUM BÉTHARRAM.
sources.incipit_latin: Dies non longe abest, ut affertur, cum indicta per te sacra sollemnitas cultores Virginis du Beau Rameau ad Bétharram congregabit
sources.notes: Source passage in this batch is the volume index (printed p. 751, 'Dies non longe. - Ad R. P. D. Franciscum M. Gieure ... occasione coronationis B. M. Virginis « du Beau Rameau », ad templum Bétharram'); the act itself was read in txt/AAS-04-1912-ocr.txt at printed p. 490, so `page` is set to 490 rather than the index page 751. The same volume's analytic index (batch passage AAS-04-1912-ocr#g771, p. 771) repeats it: 'Gieure Franciscus ... epistolam accipit, qua ei fit potestas B. M. V. « du Beau Rameau » ad Bétharram decorandi aureis coronis a beatissimo Patre oblatis, 490.' Key act wording: 'idemque binas afferet áureas coronas, quibus tibi divinae Matris Filiique effigiem, sollemnibus caeremoniis, exornandi facimus potestatem' — the Pope sends two golden crowns via Victor Bourdenne, Procurator General, and grants the diocesan bishop the faculty to crown the image of the Virgin and Child. OCR of the rubric reads 'GIBURE' for GIEURE and 'CORONATIONE' for CORONATIONIS. coronation_date: the letter (14 June 1912) says the solemnity is imminent ('Dies non longe abest'), and the index heads the letter 'occasione coronationis', so the year 1912 is stated in substance; no day/month given. Country inferred from the diocese of Bayonne, named in the rubric.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.rubric_latin: LITTERAE APOSTOLICAE quibus LEO PP. XIII gratulatur Archiepiscopo Cameracen, de felici exitu Incoronationis B. Mariae Virginis « Des Dunes ».
sources.incipit_latin: Praestans fidei ac pietatis exemplum urbe Dunkerque inter multas laetitiae demonstrationes Incoronationis Nostrae Dominae des Dunes causa excitatas
sources.notes: Papal letter of congratulation to Etienne-Marie-Alphonse (Sonnois), Archbishop of Cambrai, on the coronation of Notre-Dame des Dunes at Dunkerque; it attests the coronation rather than granting it, hence retrospective_attestation. The act is printed in French on p. 10 ('le couronnement de Notre Dame des Dunes'), with the Latin 'Versio' on p. 11 — the incipit given here is from that Versio; the French incipit after the salutation is 'L'eclatant exemple de foi et de piete donne publiquement, ces jours derniers, par la ville de Dunkerque'. No word for image/simulacrum appears: the source names only the devotional title. Coronation date not stated beyond 'ces jours derniers' / 'diebus nuper transactis' before the Datum of 10 June 1903, so only the year is recorded. Datum line: 'Donne a Rome pres Saint-Pierre, le 10 Juin 1903, de Notre Pontificat la vingt sixieme annee'. No mention of the Vatican Chapter or of a Legate. Also indexed in the volume's Summa Actorum (p. 758) and Index (p. 764) as 'de felici exitu Incoronationis B. M. V. des Dunes ... 10'. OCR of the Latin version reads 'iurganti pietatis aemulationi' (probably 'certanti'/'urgenti') and 'excitati Auctus' for 'fluctus' — repairs not applied to quoted text.

sources.act_type: Decretum (S. Congregatio Indulgentiis Sacrisque Reliquiis praeposita)
sources.legate: Archiepiscopus Bituricensis (Archbishop of Bourges; personal name not given in the text)
sources.rubric_latin: Quo conceditur ut Archisodalitas Bmae V. Mariae a « S. Corde Iesu, » ab Ecclesia S. Andreae de Valle transferri possit in Ecclesia B. Mariae V. D. Nostrae in Foro Agonali.
sources.incipit_latin: Ab anno 1854 Presbyterorum Societas Exsolduni in Archidioecesi Bituricensi in Galliis florere coepit, qui vires, consilia et operam ad vineam Domini sacris expeditionibus potissimum excolendam contulerunt
sources.notes: Decree transferring the Archconfraternity of Our Lady of the Sacred Heart from S. Andrea della Valle to the church in the Piazza Navona; it recalls in passing that the Apostolic See 'nomine proprio coronam Simulacro imponendi facultatem largita est Archiepiscopo Bituricensi' — granted the Archbishop of Bourges the faculty of imposing the crown, in the Holy See's own name, on the Issoudun image. No date is given for the grant or for the coronation itself, so coronation_date is null. Datum: 'Romae, ex Secretaria Sacrae Congregationis Indulgentiis Sacrisque Reliquiis praepositae dic 26 Aprilis 1879' ('dic' = 'die'); the act is dated 1879 although the volume (ASS 11) is labelled 1878 — the volume runs over into 1879; trusted the act. OCR repairs in the incipit: 'Exsokluni' -> 'Exsolduni', 'in Gallus' -> 'in Galliis'. Elsewhere 'Archisodalkate' -> 'Archisodalitate'. A second image, 'imago Dominae Nostrae a Sacratissimo Corde Iesu' left for public veneration at S. Andrea della Valle in Rome, is mentioned but no coronation is asserted of it, so no record was emitted for it.

sources.act_type: Epistola
sources.legate: Carolus A. de la Tour d'Auvergne, Archiepiscopus Bituricensis (crowned 'nomine decessoris Nostri f. r. Pii IX')
sources.rubric_latin: AD R. P. D. MARTINUM HIERONYMUM IZARD, ARCHIEPISCOPUM BITURICENSEM, QUINQUAGESIMO REDEUNTE ANNO CUM IMAGINI DOMINAE NOSTRAE A S. CORDE IESU IN BASILICA EXOLDUNENSI AUREA CORONA IMPOSITA EST.
sources.incipit_latin: Inter mariales aedes, quibus Gallia feliciter nobilitatur, merito sane praeclarum locum obtinet Exoldunensis Basilica
sources.notes: Letter of Benedict XV to Abp Martin Jerome Izard of Bourges for the golden jubilee of the coronation. The passage does not state the coronation year explicitly: it says the fiftieth year is about to be completed ('annus propediem expleatur quinquagesimus') since the crowning done by Abp de la Tour d'Auvergne in the name of Pius IX, and the jubilee solemnities are set for 8 September (letter dated 15 Aug 1919), hence 1869 - inferred, verify. The 'legate' field records the prelate who performed the original crowning in the Pope's name, not a legate deputed by this act. Rubric OCR read 'BITURICENSEM' as 'BITÜRICENSEM'.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.legate: Emmanuel Caelestinus S. R. E. Cardinalis Suhard, then Archbishop of Reims, later of Paris
sources.rubric_latin: ECCLESIA DEO IN HONOREM B. MARIAE V. DICATA, IN OPPIDO « LA GUERCHE DE BRETAGNE » IN GALLIA POSITA, INTRA RHEDONENSIS ARCHIDIOECESIS FINES, TITULO BASILICAE MINORIS ORNATUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Tanta in populo christiano fuit semper, inde a prioribus Ecclesiae saeculis, erga Deiparam Virginem pietas, ut haud raro quaedam urbs
sources.notes: Basilica Minor act; the clause on printed p. 725 reads: « ... quae a desideratissimo S. R. E. Presbytero Cardinali Emmanuele Caelestino Suhard, tunc Rhemensi postea Parisiensi Archiepiscopo, anno MCMXXXVII sollemni est pompa redimita ». Note that 'corona' / 'diademate' is not expressed — 'redimita' is used absolutely — so that this is a coronation is a reading of the standard AAS formula and should be verified. The vernacular title is a normalisation of the Latin 'de la Guerche' given in the text. The candidate passage is keyed to printed p. 725; the act begins on p. 724, which is cited here.

sources.notes: Basilica Minor act for Verdun cathedral; the coronation clause falls on printed p. 491, but the act opens on p. 490, so aas_page is the act's start page. Coronation clause: 'Marianum praesertim Simulacrum, quod ibidem magna devotione colitur, per Venerabilem Fratrem Angelum Iosephum Roncalli, Mesembrianum titularem Archiepiscopum, Apostolicum in Gallia Nostrum Nuntium, postridie Kalendas Iunias superiore anno, corona auro gemmisque distincta redimitum fuit.' Crowned not by a deputed Legate but by the Apostolic Nuncio to France, Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli (later John XXIII), hence 'legate' left null. coronation_date derived: 'postridie Kalendas Iunias' = 2 June; 'superiore anno' relative to the act's Datum (8 Sept 1947) = 1946 — verify. OCR of the rubric reads 'VIRDU-NENSIS' (line-break); correct form is presumably VIRODUNENSIS. Vernacular title is a rendering of the Latin 'Dominae Nostrae de Prodigiis seu de Viroduno'; not given in the text.

sources.act_type: Decretum Consistoriale (S. Congregatio Consistorialis)
sources.rubric_latin: ANCONITAN. ET HUMAN. EVECTIONIS AD DIGNITATEM ARCHIEPISCOPALEM HONORIS CAUSA. Sedes Episcopalis Anconitana evehitur in Archiepiscopalem honoris causa.
sources.incipit_latin: Honoribus et privilegiis cumulare civitates tum incolarum frequentia tum nobilitate conspicuas, eas praesertim quae ab aetate Apostolica christianam fidem amplexatae sunt
sources.notes: Retrospective mention of a personal papal coronation, on printed p. 198: 'quamque gloriosus Pontifex Pius VII, Savona ubi captivus fuerat rediens, suis manibus aurea corona donavit.' Crowned by Pius VII with his own hands on his return from captivity at Savona; no date is given in the text (Pius VII's return journey was in 1814), so coronation_date is null. Page set to 195, where the decree begins ('EX S. CONGREGATIONE CONSISTORIALI - ANCONITAN. ET HUMAN.'); the coronation statement is on p. 198 and the Datum (14 September 1904) on p. 200 - rubric, incipit and date taken from the full volume text. Country derived from Ancona/Picenum/Adriatic. OCR running head reads 'Ancoriitan.'.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.rubric_latin: TITULUS ET PRIVILEGIA BASILICAE MINORIS CONFERUNTUR METROPOLITANAE ECCLESIAE S. CYRIACI EP. M. ANCONAE, SACRIS RELIQUIIS ET PRODIGIIS PRAECLARAE.
sources.incipit_latin: Metropolitanum Anconae templum in excelso civitatis colle situm, late mare prospiciens Hadriacum, saeculo octavo exeunte traditur fuisse erectum
sources.notes: The passage itself is the volume's Index rerum analyticus (printed p. 491), whose entry reads 'Pius PP. VII, 201; redimivit corona imaginem Reginae omnium Sanctorum, Anconae, 14'. Verified against the act in the same volume file: the Litterae Apostolicae raising the metropolitan church of Ancona to a minor basilica begin on printed p. 13 and state on p. 14 'Imaginem thaumaturgam titulo Reginae Sanctorum omnium excultam, a captivitate redux sa. me. Pius PP. VII Praedecessor Noster, maxima populi ac civitatis laetitia, aurea gemmataque corona sollemni pompa redimivit'. So the crowning was performed personally by Pius VII after his return from captivity (i.e. after 1814; no date given - coronation_date null); it is here reported retrospectively inside a basilica-minor act of Pius XI, hence retrospective_attestation rather than papal_personal_coronation. The image is a Marian image painted on linen on one of the principal altars. Datum line: 'die xiv mensis Iulii anno MDCCCCXXVI'. page set to 13 (act begins) though the coronation sentence and the index citation are on p. 14. Country 'Italy' inferred from Ancona / 'inter sacras Piceni aedes'; confidence dropped to medium for that reason only - the coronation fact itself is explicit.

sources.incipit_latin: Ex quo, anno scilicet proxime praeterito, praeclara Imago Beatae Mariae Virginis a Gratiis, quae in sacrario apud Basilicam cathedralem Asculanam in Piceno asservatur
sources.notes: Patron declaration opening 'Ex quo, anno scilicet proxime praeterito, praeclara Imago ... auctoritate Petriani Canonicorum Collegii, aureo diademate fuit redimita'. Coronation year 1960 derived from 'anno proxime praeterito' relative to the act date. The Datum line is OCR'd 'die XXVIII mensis Aprilis, anno m c m x x i' — MCMXXI is an OCR corruption of MCMLXI (1961), confirmed by 'Pontificatus Nostri tertio' and the volume year. Country Italy inferred from Asculum in Piceno; not stated.

register_refs: Raffaelli Sinodo Lib. II. MS. nell' Arch. Vat.no Capitolare pag. 45. §. XXXI
sources.rubric_latin: Dell' Immagine di Maria detta la Madonna del Lago, che si venera nella Chiesa situata fuori di Bertinoro
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'duas Coronas aureas ponderis Scutor. Quadraginta unius cum dimidio auri'. Petitioner: Abbate Francesco Giacinto Ascensini, Provost of the cathedral of Bertinoro (original instances to the Chapter); execution then solicited by Bishop Missiroli in May 1705 and by Abbot Vitale Ascevolini of S. Maria d'Urano. Place-name OCR forms: 'Brecinoca' (f.2r silversmith account), 'Brictinorii', 'Brittinorij', 'Britonorij', 'Ber-gamoro'; abbey 'de Urano' also OCR'd as 'de Trano', 'de Prano'. Concession date 1689-06-20 comes from the margin note '20. Junii 1689 conced.' on the near-empty title leaf f.5v ('Conc[essione] dell'Ill'mo e R'mo Capitolo di S. Pietro delle Corone d'oro', signed 'Gio: Giardini Agt.o'); the crowns' inscription and the 1789 engraving say the crown was donated 'Anno 1704', and the Chapter's delegation letter is dated Rome 13 June 1705. Coronation on the theatre in the piazza of Bertinoro on 9 Aug 1705 (instrument 'die nona mensis Augusti' 1705; printed relazione: feasts 8-11 Aug 1705, crowning on Sunday). Documents in order: f.2r silversmith's account (two crowns, 41.5 scudi); f.3r-4r extract from Raffaelli's MS synod with instrument summary ('other'); f.5v concession title leaf ('decretum'); f.6r-16r printed 'Vera, e distinta relazione' (Cesena, Demetrio Degni, 1705) with an inserted 1789 engraving by Cavallucci/Bombelli; f.17r inserted printed odes for the 1805 centenary (one copy OCR'd as '1826'/'1851', likely misread); f.19r-22r notarial instrument of donation and receipt by Petrus Dominicus Toninus, incorporating the Chapter's letter of 13 June 1705 and the monks' mandate of 8 Aug 1705; f.22v bishop's attestation of the notary, 27 Aug 1705, with archivist margin note 'Inś Declarationis ... Die 9. Augś 1705' and 'Caps: 39. fasc: 309'; f.23r-v bishop's letter of thanks to the Chapter, Bertinoro 27 Aug 1705, in two copies (second copy dateline OCR'd 'Ostiglia', signature 'Cristoforo Vin.co Di Berrini' garbled). The two register refs 'Caps. 29. f. 379' and 'Caps: 39. fasc: 309' probably refer to the same instrument with an OCR discrepancy.

sources.rubric_latin: Eminentissimo Archiepiscopo Bononiensi Breve, quo indulgentiae quaedam a Sanctissimo conceduntur.
sources.incipit_latin: Qui vel a teneris annis singulari obsequio, intimoque cordis affectu sanctam Dei Genitricem Mariam coluimus
sources.notes: Pius IX grants the Cardinal Archbishop of Bologna, 'tamquam Delegatum Nostrum', the faculty to place a golden crown 'Nostro nomine' on the image on 15 August of the current year ('hoc vertente anno, die decimaquinta mensis Augusti'); since the Brief is dated 16 July 1875, the coronation date is 1875-08-15. The delegate is addressed only as 'Venerabilis Frater' / 'Eminentissimo Archiepiscopo Bononiensi' and is not named, hence legate: null. OCR: 'supradicto cognationis die' read as 'coronationis die'; 'translatant' for 'translatam'. Volume 9 = 1876 but the Brief is of 1875. Country derived from 'Bononiae'.

sources.act_type: Causa apud S. Congregationem Rituum (concessio et approbatio Officii et Missae propriae) cum informatione praevia
sources.rubric_latin: INSULAE SARDINIAE. CONCESSIONIS ET APPROBATIONIS OFFICII ET MISSAE PROPRIAE IN HONOREM B. V. A BONO AERE NUNCUPATAE.
sources.incipit_latin: Antequam referam S. Congregationis Decretum, nonnulla indicabo, quae ostendunt, quomodo solent eiusmodi causae pertractari
sources.notes: Key sentence, on printed p. 354: 'Insignis haec B. Virginis imago ex Capituli Vaticani Decreto die 24 Aprilis 1870 aurea corona rite decorata est.' Crowning by the Chapter of St Peter's (Capitulum Vaticanum). Page set to 353, where the item ('INSULAE SARDINIAE ...') begins; the coronation statement is on p. 354. The passage is the editorial 'Brevis informatio' preceding the S.R.C. decree, hence incipit_latin is the editorial opening, not an act body. Vernacular title taken from the Italian book cited in the text ('Della statua miracolosa di Maria Vergine di Bonaria'). Volume 6 spans 1870-71; the related decree is dated 22 April 1871. Country derived from 'in Sardiniae insula' / 'Calarim'. OCR of the rubric reads 'A BONO AÈRE'.

sources.incipit_latin: Insignis admodum ac perantiqua est Marialis aedes quae, in Calaritana urbe sita, a Bono Aere nuncupatur
sources.notes: Re-coronation after the sacrilegious theft of the crowns of the Virgin and the Child three years earlier (c. 1923): 'te ... his Litteris eligimus qui coronam auream simulacro Virginis de Bono Aere nomine et auctoritate Nostra imponas'. The act also attests the earlier crowning by the Vatican Chapter ('a Vaticano Capitulo corona aurea redimita sit', dated 1870 by AAS 18 [1926] 376). Coronation year 1926 inferred: the solemnities were being prepared at the date of the letter (25 March 1926) and the new church was inaugurated 22 April 1926 per AAS 18 (1926) 376.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.rubric_latin: SANCTUARIUM B. M. V. DE BONARIA CALARITANAE CIVITATIS IN BASILICAM MINOREM EVEHITUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Calaritana in civitate ac dioecesi sanctuarium Beatae Mariae Virginis de Bonaria nuncupatae exstat, curis religiosorum sodalium ex Ordine Beatae Mariae Virginis de Mercede concreditum
sources.notes: 'in quo antiqua et prodigiosa Virginis effigies, iam aureo diademate anno MDCCCLXX per decretum Capituli Vaticani redimita, colitur'. Same image as AAS 18 (1926) 302. The act also notes the inauguration of the new church on 22 April 1926 and the 1908 proclamation of the Virgin of Bonaria as principal patron of Sardinia by Pius X.

sources.citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 242r–245v
sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, instrumentum donationis, other
sources.legate: the diocesan bishop, who imposed the crown in pontificals (name OCR-garbled: 'Ill.mus D. Card.lis Octavianus Acciaioli ... Ep.o Vercellensis')
sources.deputy: the diocesan bishop, who imposed the crown in pontificals (name OCR-garbled: 'Ill.mus D. Card.lis Octavianus Acciaioli ... Ep.o Vercellensis')
sources.rubric_latin: in Ecclesia Parochiali B. M. Virginis Mariæ Fontis Miraculorum Caravaggii Cremonen. diœcesis
sources.notes: Crowns: one ('una Corona d'Oro Grande Tonda all'imperiale ... per la Ill.ma Madonna di Caravaggio'). Conto (242r): one crown weighing 128 scudi 2 den. 12 gr. of gold, total 257:55, 100 scudi paid on account by 12 July, signed off by Amato Vannini 'Can.co Deput.o'. Instrument (243r-244r): 'Die Lunæ vigesima nona Mensis Septembris' 1710, Clement XI year 10 (weekday checks); crown placed 'Super Caput Statuæ ejusdem Almæ Virginis Mariæ S.ctæ Miraculorum' by the bishop; the Latin is heavily garbled (Cremonese canons named: Maynoldi, Sforza, Cambiago, Tesauro; cardinal-legate and 'Regio Magistratu' present); followed by the 'Ordo Servandus in Coronandis Coronis aureis' and Cremona chancery authentications (244v, dated 19 Apr 1709 in one OCR copy and 26 Jul 1690 in the other). The concession date 1709-04-15 comes from the margin note 'Conceditur ac mandatur confici auream coronam Die 15 Aprilis 1709' on the conto cover at 245v (Giardini signature), assigned to Caravaggio because it sits between this dossier and the Frascati one and speaks of a single crown; medium confidence. Margin 'N. C. 26.' at 243v may be a register reference. 242v is an illegible Latin page.

legates: Adeodatus Ioannes Piazza, S.R.E. Cardinalis, Patriarch of Venice

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.legate: Adeodatus Ioannes Piazza, S.R.E. Cardinalis, Patriarch of Venice
sources.rubric_latin: ECCLESIA PAROECIALIS, GODII IN ARCE MANTUANAE DIOECESIS EXTANS, DEO IN HONOREM B. MARIAE V. VULGO « MADONNA DELLA SALUTE » DICATA, BASILICIS MINORIBUS ACCENSETUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Ut pretiosissima gemma in aureo anulo sic Ecclesia, in qua pervetusta Imago Beatae Mariae Virginis sub titulo v. « Madonna della Salute » ditissimo fulget diademate
sources.notes: Basilica Minor act recording a coronation carried out in the Pope's name: 'ditissimo fulget diademate Eidem sollemniter imposito Nostro Nomine die iv mensis Novembris superioris anni a Dilecto Filio Nostro Adeodato Ioanne S.R.E. Presbytero Cardinali Piazza, Venetiarum Patriarcha' — and later 'auctoritate Nostra, per similes Apostolicas Litteras die xxix mensis Octobris eiusdem anni sub anulo Piscatoris datas, aurea corona gemmata ... sollemniter redimita est fictilis perantiqua Imago'. 'superioris anni' relative to the act (15 Aug 1946) gives 4 Nov 1945; the enabling Apostolic Letters are dated 29 Oct 1945. Terracotta image found within the walls of the castle of Godium in 1702, popularly 'del terraglio'. Passage printed_page was 447; act begins on printed p. 445. 'Godium' is Castel Goffredo (Mantua) — identification inferred from 'Godii in arce ... in ripa Mincii ... Gonzaga Marchionum'.

sources.act_type: Decretum Consistoriale (S. Congregatio Consistorialis) - erectio in Basilicam minorem
sources.rubric_latin: CLAVAREN. ERECTIONIS AD DIGNITATEM BASILICAE MINORIS. Cathedralis ecclesia B. M. Virgini de Horto Clavara sacra in Basilicam minorem erigitur.
sources.incipit_latin: Inter aedes augustae Dei Genitrici in Liguria dicatas ea sane memoratu digna est quae Clavarii existit Beatae Virgini ab Horto nuncupatae sacra
sources.notes: Retrospective clause on printed p. 479: '... eam anno MDCXLV urbis Clavarii praesides ac finitimorum pagorum magistratus, cunctis plaudentibus, in caelestem civitatis ac totius Clavarensis regionis Praestitem delegerint, atque Vaticanum Capitulum sacram Imaginem aurea corona donandam decreverit.' Crowning decreed by the Chapter of St Peter's (Capitulum Vaticanum). Confidence medium because the year MDCXLV = 1645 is stated primarily of the patronal election, and it is only by the construction of the sentence that it also covers the Chapter's decree; a checker should verify the coronation year. Page set to 478, where the decree begins (the coronation statement is on p. 479; rubric line 'CLAVAREN. ERECTIONIS AD DIGNITATEM BASILICAE MINORIS' taken from the full volume text). OCR: 'Clavara' for 'Clavarii'/'Clavarensi', 'moHtionibus' for 'molitionibus'. Country: 'in Liguria' explicit.

sources.citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 70r–73v
sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: instrumentum donationis, lettera, supplica
sources.legate: R.mus D. Melchior [surname garbled], canon of the Vatican Basilica, ex Cubicularius honoris of Clement XI, 'specialiter deputatus'
sources.deputy: R.mus D. Melchior [surname garbled], canon of the Vatican Basilica, ex Cubicularius honoris of Clement XI, 'specialiter deputatus'
sources.rubric_latin: Immagine della Madonna S.ma di Cibona, ò M.te Vrbano, Diocese di Sutri venerata nella Chiesa de PP. Eremiti del M.te Senario che habitano nel Sac. Eremo denominato di Cibona
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Infant Jesus) — 'duas Coronas aureas ... coronandi vera Simulacra ... Beat.mæ Virginis ejusq. SS.mi Infantis Jesu'. Petitioner: The Hermits of Monte Senario at the Eremo di Cibona ('Istanza ... 1690'), with an attestation letter of 'Fran.co Vesc.o di Subi.o Neri' (probably Francesco, bishop of Sutri e Nepi) dated 8 May 1690. The bishop's letter (f. 70r-71r, dated 'Stegi 8. Maggio 1690' — 'Stegi' is probably OCR for Nepi; signature 'Vesc.o di Subi.o Neri' read as 'Vescovo di Sutri e Nepi') attests the three conditions: painted c. 1462 at the expense of Agostino Chigi, alum-works contractor, for the alum-mine workers; miracles registered to no. 1223 (or 3000); given in custody to the hermits by Urban VIII in 1633; never crowned. f. 71v docket: 'Istanza Per la Coronazione della Sac. Immagine della Bma. Verg. Maria del M. Urbano Diocesi di Sut[ri] 1690' with annotations 'Suis loc. et tempore corona[bitur]' and 'Scribat S[ecreta]rio' — so the 1690 date is that of the request/deferred concession, not an explicit 'conceditur'. The instrument (f. 72r-73r) is dated 1 June 1704, Clement XI year 4, drawn up 'in mansione Cap.li eiusd. Erem.i'; it records the crowns weighed at 'centum du[o] et unius denarij aurei' and that the simulacra were carried to the church and crowned before a great multitude; accepted by 'R. P. f. Amadeus ... Rector ejusd. Eremij'; notary 'Horatius ... Suentius' (garbled). The archivist's margin note at f. 73v reads 'Instrum. Donationis Duarum Coronarum aurearum factae ... simulacro miraculoso B. M. V. ... in Ven. Eccl. Sacri Eremi RR. PP. Eremitarum ... in Terr[itorio] [T]olphae; die 18 Junij 1[7]84' — OCR gives '1784', impossible for this volume, and '18 Junij' conflicts with the instrument's 'prima Junii'; the instrument date is preferred. Country inferred from Sutri/Tolfa.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.legate: Fodianus Ordinarius (Iosephus Lenotti, Archiepiscopus Fodianus, was the petitioner and is charged to impose the crown 'Nostro nomine et auctoritate')
sources.rubric_latin: Sinitur pretioso diademate redimiri imago Beatae Mariae Virginis vulgo Iconavetere nuncupata, quae in cathedrali templo metropolitanae Ecclesiae Fodianae exstat.
sources.incipit_latin: Cum ducentesimus et quinquagesimus feliciter recurreret annus impletus ex quo fideles Fodiani mariali, ut fertur, prodigio sunt ditati
sources.notes: Opens 'Ad futuram rei memoriam' (not 'Ad perpetuam'). The act itself attests an EARLIER coronation of the same image: 'secundum etiam revolveretur saeculum postquam imago Beatae Mariae Virginis vulgo Iconavetere appellata a Petriano Canonicorum Collegio coronata est' - i.e. the second centenary of a crowning by the Vatican Chapter, so c. 1781; the exact year is not given. Occasion also the 250th year since the Marian prodigy at Foggia. Country Italy inferred from the see of Foggia (Fodiana); not stated in the act. Coronation day left to the Ordinary's choice. Confirmed in the volume indices at pp. 757 and 776.

sources.legate: Mons. Guido del Palagio (de Balagio / del Baglio), Patrizio Romano, canonico della Basilica Vaticana, Referendario di Segnatura
sources.deputy: Mons. Guido del Palagio (de Balagio / del Baglio), Patrizio Romano, canonico della Basilica Vaticana, Referendario di Segnatura
sources.rubric_latin: Instrum Donationis Duar. Coronar. aurear. valoris 409 ... imaginib. miraculosis B. M. V. de Planchis, et Pueri Iesu existent. in Eccl. ... Societatis sub invocat. eiusd. ssmae Virginis de Planchis, et S.ti Leonardi Civitatis Fulginei p. die XIV. mensis Majj 1716
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child), 'all'Imperiale', valued 409:81 scudi. Petitioner: Confraternita / Archiconfraternita della Madonna del Pianto e S. Leonardo di Foligno (Governatore Francesco Silvestri, Guardiani Filippo Giusti and Vincenzo Bussaroni, 1704; Governatore Giovanni Battista Marcelli, 1713). Image is a dressed wooden statue of the Virgin seated with the Child (attestation of 9 Aug 1704, notary Giovanni Scarpellini, with a drawing 'accluso' and notes on the silver crown/star at f. 272v). Documents: sworn attestation of origin and miracles (earthquake of 14 Jan 1703) 1704 = 'other'; an undated letter (f. 271r) asking the Canons for a 'dilazione' so the feast of coronation could wait for the new church ('dentro il Mese di Mag. 1702', '1703') - implies the concession predates 1704 but no decree date is given, hence concession_date null; mandate to Giardini (f. 277r) 'p. la Ma.da SS.ma della Terr.a di Foligno'; conto Giardini 20 May 1713 (OCR 'Fulignio', later dates '1623' = 1713); Latin instrumentum of donation Actum in the Cathedral of Foligno 14 May 1713 (Sunday), attested by the bishop 'Aloisius Malvitius Fontana' 22 May 1713; relazione headed (OCR) 'il 23: Maggio 1723 da Monsig.r Ill.mo Guido del Baglio' - read 1713; relazione text fixes the day as 'quatordici del Mese di Maggio', Sunday after vespers, the day after 'Sabbato 23 [=13]'. Margin note 272v adds 'Dicembre' after 1713, unexplained. The relazione runs on past f. 285r. Piratello letters (ff. 273r-275r) are interleaved inside this folio span. | Range opens mid-way through the Italian relazione of the ceremony (begins before pb 673); the deputy is called only 'Mons.r Ill.mo Incoronante' and is never named in these pages. Relazione: Saturday 23 May, first vespers sung by 'Mon Sig: Malavicini' Bishop of Foligno (name OCR-uncertain), coronation performed the following Sunday after vespers in the Cathedral of S. Feliciano, statues of Mother and Child crowned, De profundis for Count Sforza, procession the following Tuesday. 23 May fell on a Saturday only in 1716 among nearby years, so coronation = Sunday 24 May 1716; the margin note's instrument date 'XIV. mensis Majj 1716' is probably OCR for XXIV. 'de Planchis' = de Planctu (Madonna del Pianto). 'Caps. B 9' probably 'Caps. 29'. Only margin notes survive for ff. 287r-289v; f.289v also carries the head 'Conto ... delle Corone d'Oro' with signature 'Gio: Giardin Argentiere' (silversmith's account, text not transcribed).

sources.rubric_latin: Ecclesia SS. Rosarii B. M. V. oppidi Fontanellato dioecesis Parmensis erigitur in Basilicam minorem.
sources.incipit_latin: Extat intra fines Parmensis dioeceseos in oppido, cui nomen vulgo Fontanellato, sacra aedes Deo in honorem Sacratissimo Rosarii Beatae Mariae Virginis dicata
sources.notes: Retrospective clause: 'in qua vetus ipsius Deiparae Virginis colitur simulacrum, clarum prodigiis atque aurea corona gemmisque distincta anno 1660 redimitum.' Confidence lowered to medium because the text does NOT say by whose authority the crown was conferred (no mention of the Vatican Chapter or of a papal indult), so the papal-authority element is unattested here; a checker should verify. OCR: 'distincta' for 'distinctum'/'distinct[a corona]'; 'honorii!centias' for 'honorificentias'. Country derived from 'dioecesis Parmensis' / 'ex Aemilia ... ex aliis Italiae regionibus'.

sources.rubric_latin: AD EM.UM P. D. EUGENIUM, TIT. SS. SILVESTRI ET MARTINI, S. R. E. PRESB. CARD. TOSI ARCHIEPISCOPUM MEDIOLANENSEM, QUEM DELIGIT LEGATUM SUUM AD CORONAS IMPONENDAS INFANTI IESU ET BEATAE VIRGINI DE FONTANELLATO, IN DIOECESI PARMENSI.
sources.incipit_latin: Quod Sanctuarii de Fontanellato laus ac fama non modo in dioecesis Parmensis totiusque Aemiliae finibus percrebrescit, sed etiam apud exteras gentes
sources.notes: Single statue group: crowns for both the Virgin and the Infant Jesus she carries ('coronas ... Virgini de Fontanellato et Infanti Iesu, quem Ipsa in ulnis sustinet, veluti manibus Nostris imponas'), the Pope himself blessing the crowns beforehand. Solemnities set for May 1925 ('sacris sollemnibus mense maio Parmae habendis'), hence coronation_date 1925. The act also records earlier crownings in 1660 and 1771 ('quam annis MDCLX et MDCCLXXI factum est'). Vernacular title supplied from the place name; the act gives only 'Virgo de Fontanellato'.

sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, decretum, instrumentum donationis, other, relazione, stampa
sources.legate: Faustino Crispolti, Canon of the Vatican Basilica, Referendary and Auditor of Card. Spinola (deputed by Chapter 22 Oct 1713)
sources.deputy: Faustino Crispolti, Canon of the Vatican Basilica, Referendary and Auditor of Card. Spinola (deputed by Chapter 22 Oct 1713)
sources.rubric_latin: Instru. Donationis duar. Coronar. aurear. ... fact. Imaginibus miraculosis B. M. V. et Pueri Jesu d. S. Maria di Capo d'Oca in civitate Tusculana die 20. xbr. 1713 — Caps. 39. fasc. 329
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Dossier contents: notarial extract of the 1703 Apostolic Visitation of Frascati (Abp. F. M. de Rubeis) describing the mural image 'B. M. V. Puerum gestantis in muro depicta' in S. Mariæ Capitis Crucis of the Theatines, translated 5 May 1613, extract dated 18 Dec 1709 (246r-v); Giardini conto for two imperial crowns, 111 scudi of gold, total 228:30, paid 215 scudi from 2 Nov 1713 to 11 Oct 1714 (247r); instrument of consignment by notary Pietro Ignazio Lelli, Frascati, 28 Oct 1713 (248r-249r), archivist summary at 249v (OCR reads 'Capo d'Oca' and '20. xbr.' for Capocroce / 28 8br); conto cover with 'Decretum 11 9bris 1709' (250v) and filing note '1709 51 / Frascati de' PP. Teatini' (251v); relazione of the coronation (252r-253v); engravings by Giovan Franceschini 'Vera Effigie della Miracolosa Vergine ... detta di Capocroce' (254r; the 1813 reprint at 256r); 1819 commemorative inscription 'MEMORIAE ET POSTERITATI' recording the crown given 'IV KAL. NOVEMBRIS' 1713, copied by Mons. D'Achille 9 Oct 1855 (254v-255v). Coronation date: relazione and instrument give Saturday 28 Oct 1713; one engraving caption reads '11. di Settembre 1713' (probably OCR/engraver variant). The crowns were fixed on the images by P. Filippo Maria Trigoni/Triconi, Theatine. Petitioner not stated in range (Theatine fathers, Vicar Guglielmo della Valle, received the crowns). '1709 51' / 'origine N. 51' at 251v may be a further filing reference.

sources.act_type: Epistola
sources.legate: Thomas Pius S. R. E. Card. Boggiani, Archbishop of Genoa
sources.rubric_latin: AD THOMAM PIUM S. R. E. PRESB. CARD. BOGGIANI, ARCHIEPISCOPUM IANUENSEM, QUI DELEGATUR A B. P. UT EIUS NOMINE SIMULACRUM DEIPARAE A VINEIS AUREA CORONA REDIMIAT ET BENEDICTIONEM IMPERTIAT CUM INDULGENTIA PLENARIA.
sources.incipit_latin: Quae civitatis istius, pastorali studio tuo commissae, propius intersint, ea planum est sic ad Nos pertinere
sources.notes: Benedict XV delegates Card. Boggiani to crown the marble image in his name ('hoc tibi munus delegamus, ut, nomine Nostro, et effigiem Deiparae a Vineis aurea, quam memoravimus, corona redimias'). Coronation date derived from 'ea in diem primum ac vicesimum vertentis mensis, qui dies Deiparae a Vineis sacer est ... indixistis' in a letter dated 1 November 1920, hence 21 November 1920 - verify. This is the fourth centennial crowning: Abp Orazio Spinola first crowned the image in 1616 ('anno MDCXVI ... diademate primum ornasse'), with the rite to be repeated every hundred years; the 1916 centenary was deferred because of the war. Benedict XV, baptized in this parish church, donated the golden crown.

images.image_title_latin: Sancta Maria Liberatrix ('sub Invocatione Sanctę Marię Liberatricis')
images.church_or_sanctuary: chapel (sacellum) of the Metropolitan church of Genoa (Ecclesię Metropolitanę Januensi)

sources.citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 177r–177v
sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: decretum, other
sources.rubric_latin: Capitulo Ecclesię Metropolitanę Januensi ... Sanctę Imaginis Beatiss.mę Virginis asservatę in Sacello eiusdem Metropolitanę, quę colitur sub Invocatione Sanctę Marię Liberatricis Auream Coronam eidem concessa fuit
sources.notes: Crowns: one ('Auream Coronam eidem concessa fuit'). Petitioner: Archbishop, Senate and Chapter of the Metropolitan church of Genoa (Archiepiscopo, Senatui et Capitulo Ecclesię Metropolitanę Januensi). Single leaf: certificate of the Chapter secretary (Alexander Chiavelli[?] Can. & Secret.), dated 22 Nov 1742, attesting that in the extraordinary capitular congregation of 9 Sept 1742 the gold crown was conceded, 'habendam tamen suis loco et tempore et pro nunc faciendam sumptibus praesentium' (crown to be made for now at the petitioners' expense). Margin note reads '113 175' and '~ S. Maria in Vico ~', which does not match the text; f.177v margin 'R. 118'. 'Januensi' (Genoa) is the OCR reading; note that the following dossier concerns the Palermo Cathedral statue 'S. Maria Libera Inferni', whose printed history glosses the name as 'Liberatrice dal Purgatorio' - it is possible this certificate actually concerns Palermo (Metropolitan church, Senate, chapel, immemorial cult) and 'Januensi' is an OCR error; cannot be verified. The label leaf f.178v ('351', 'Decretum 23 Febr. 1699') sits between this record and the Palermo dossier; its attribution is uncertain.

sources.incipit_latin: Fortiter suaviterque ad ineundas religionis semitas immo et sacerdotii Divinam Misericordiam Nos a teneris annis impulisse, iuvat nunc grato animo meminisse

sources.act_type: Epistula
sources.rubric_latin: E.mo P. D. Ioanni Baptistae S. R. E. Cardinali Montini, Archiepiscopo Mediolanensi, qui in oppido v. « Imbersago » interfuit sollemnibus, quibus statua aenea Ioanni Pp. XXIII posita est in sacra Aede B. Mariae Virg. v. « Madonna del Bosco » appellatae.
sources.incipit_latin: Con soave pensiero l'animo si volge al Santuario della Madonna del Bosco, che soffuse su la Nostra infanzia un ineffabile sorriso di cielo
sources.notes: Letter in Italian to Card. Montini. John XXIII recalls: 'il 29 agosto 1954, con la cerimonia della solenne incoronazione della sacra effigie, ivi venerata, che Ci fu dato di compiere in nome e per procura del Cardinale Arcivescovo Schuster'. IMPORTANT for a checker: the writer (then Patriarch of Venice, not yet Pope) performed the crowning as proxy for Cardinal Schuster, Archbishop of Milan; the text does NOT state papal or Vatican Chapter authority for the coronation, so 'papal_personal_coronation' is used only in the literal sense that the reigning Pope personally performed it. Rubric OCR reads « Imfoersago » — repaired to « Imbersago ». Diocese (Milan) inferred from the addressee and from Card. Schuster; country inferred from Brianza/Lombardy. The letter opens on printed page 850; the coronation clause falls on page 851.

sources.act_type: Epistula
sources.rubric_latin: E.mo P. D. Ioanni Baptistae S. R. E. Cardinali Montini, Archiepiscopo Mediolanensi, qui in oppido v. « Imbersago » interfuit sollemnibus, quibus statua aenea Ioanni Pp. XXIII posita est in sacra Aede B. Mariae Virg. v. « Madonna del Bosco » appellatae.
sources.notes: The Pope recalls 'la cerimonia della solenne incoronazione della sacra effigie, ivi venerata, che Ci fu dato di compiere in nome e per procura del Cardinale Arcivescovo Schuster' on 29 August 1954 — i.e. the crowning was performed by Angelo Roncalli (then Patriarch of Venice, not yet Pope) as proxy for Cardinal Ildefonso Schuster, Archbishop of Milan, the day before Schuster's death. Hence retrospective_attestation, not papal_personal_coronation. OCR of the rubric reads 'Imfoersago'; read as 'Imbersago'. Act begins on printed page 850; passage page 851. Body in Italian, no Latin incipit.

sources.citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 257r–275r
sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, decretum, instrumentum donationis, lettera, other, relazione
sources.legate: Mons. Giovanni Andrea Ricci, canonico di S. Pietro
sources.deputy: Mons. Giovanni Andrea Ricci, canonico di S. Pietro
sources.rubric_latin: Instro della Coronat.ne di due Corone d'oro fatta all'Imagino della SS.ma Vergine, e Bambino Giesù detta del Piratello esistente nella Chiesa dei PP. del T. ord.e di S. Fran.co fuori della Città d'Imola
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Petitioner: the Franciscans of the Third Order (P. Generale Paolo Lombardini; P. Maestro F. Elia) and other superiors of the church, who requested the crowns in advance. Giardini conto (257r): two crowns weighing 37 scudi 2 den. of gold, worked with foliage and cherub heads, total 83 scudi, settled at 78 scudi; the sum was advanced by the General of the Franciscan Third Order to be refunded by the Chapter 'quando avvinarà il tempo e il Luogo nel quale doveano darsi dette Corone'. Conto cover with 'Decretum die Lunae 2 9brjs 1711' (258v; 2 Nov 1711 was a Monday). Payment order by Amato Vannini, Canon Dean, 10 Dec 1713 ('come a ciò deputato', probably as the Chapter's deputy for the crowns rather than the crowning deputy) and Giardini's receipt dated Dec 1713 (259r). No coronation or instrument in range; the dossier ends at the last page of the batch, so it likely continues. OCR spells the town 'Immola' / 'Imola'. | Dossier is interleaved with the Foligno one: Piratello material at ff. 257r-267r.02 (conto Giardini 78 scudi for the two crowns, paid 10 Dec 1713 by the Franciscan Third Order general; margin 'Decretum die Lunae 2 9brjs 1711' on the conto sheet, taken as the concession decree - 2 Nov 1711 was a Monday, but the decree could instead concern the payment; instrument of quittance 'Actum Imolae in Platea Publica' 15 Aug 1714 = 'Die Mercurij ... Decima quinta mensis Augusti', Wednesday, consistent; relazione of the triduo 14-16 Aug 1714 with the crowning on Assumption Day; two copies of Card. Gozzadini's thank-you letter, OCR-dated '9bre 1712', surely 1714) and again at ff. 273r-275r (Ricci's covering letter 'Imola 19 Agosto 1714'; archivist note at 274v; margin fragment at 275r). OCR gives the archivist's head at 261v as 'li 25 Ag.to 1714' and 274v 'Sotto li 29 Ag.to 1714' - read 15 and 19. Ricci's deputation is OCR-dated '5. marzo 1723' (read 1714). Image: painting on terracotta venerated since 1488. Cardinal named 'Forzadori' in OCR = Gozzadini. f. 267v.01 is an unrelated misfiled 1618 supplica about a canon of Cosenza. f. 275r also carries a 1717 order to pay Giardini for 'l'ultima Corona d'oro' naming no image.

sources.rubric_latin: AD EM.UM P. D. PETRUM, TIT. SANCTI LAURENTII IN LUCINA, S. R. E. PRESB. CARDINALEM GASPARRI, A NEGOTIIS PUBLICIS ADMINISTRUM, QUEM LEGATUM MITTIT AD TRANSVEHENDAM LAURETUM BEATAE MARIAE VIRGINIS NOVAM ICONEM, A SE BENEDICTAM AUREOQUE DIADEMATE REDIMITAM.
sources.incipit_latin: Norunt omnes quo maerore affectus sit orbis catholicus, cum, haud ita pridem, Lauretana aede ardescente, imago illa augustissima Beatae Mariae Virginis penitus deleta est
sources.notes: The new statue made after the 1921 fire: 'cum Ipsi simulacrum novum Mariae et Iesu diademate aureo ditaverimus, tum idem sollemni ritu benedictum coronavimus' - Pius XI crowned it himself in Rome before 17 Aug 1922. Card. Gasparri is deputed as Legate only to convey the image to Loreto, not to crown it. Country inferred from Loreto/Lauretum (unambiguous); diocese not named in the act.

sources.act_type: Litterae Encyclicae
sources.rubric_latin: AD VENERABILES FRATRES PATRIARCHAS, PRIMATES, ARCHIEPISCOPOS, EPISCOPOS, ALIOSQUE LOCORUM ORDINARIOS PACEM ET COMMUNIONEM CUM APOSTOLICA SEDE HABENTES: DE PACE CHRISTI IN REGNO CHRISTI QUAERENDA.
sources.incipit_latin: Ubi arcano Dei consilio ac nutu Nos, qui nullis sane meritis commendaremur, ad hanc et veritatis cathedram et caritatis evecti sumus
sources.notes: Encyclical 'Ubi arcano Dei consilio', which begins on printed p. 673; the coronation reference is on p. 675 (the passage page): 'venerabile ipsius simulacrum, apud Nos affabre refectum, Nostrisque manibus et consecratum et corona redimitum, restituendum curavimus'. Rubric and incipit taken from p. 673 of the same volume text. Same image as AAS 14 (1922) 544. Country inferred (Loreto).

sources.act_type: Epistola
sources.rubric_latin: AD R. P. D. ALPHONSUM ANDREOLI, EPISCOPUM RECINETENSEM ET LAURETANUM, QUINQUAGESIMO PLENO ANNO AB INITO SACERDOTIO.
sources.incipit_latin: Cum allatum ad Nos sit, quinquagesimum sacerdotii natalem a te propediem actum iri, placet in partem venire, ut aequum est, gaudii laetitiaeque tuae
sources.notes: Act VIII begins on printed p. 215 (the passage page marker is 216). Attests in passing: 'populi pietas in novam Virginis Effigiem, quam Nosmet ipsi lustravimus et corona redimivimus'. Coronation year 1922 taken from the parallel acts AAS 14 (1922) 544 and 675, not stated here; country inferred (Loreto).

sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, decretum, instrumentum donationis, lettera, other, relazione

sources.deputy: Abbate Gio. Andrea Ricci (Abbas Joannes Andreas Riccius, Politianus, canon of St Peter's), delegate of the Vatican Chapter
sources.rubric_latin: Relazione del seguito nella Venuta dell'Illmo e Rmo Sig.r Can.co Gio. Andrea Ricci in Montepulciano per coronare la Bma Vergine detta di S. Martino esistente nella Chiesa Cattedrale
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'duas coronas aureas valoris et aestimationis scut. centum monetae Romanae'. f.188r: letter of Gio. Andrea Ricci from Montepulciano, 31 Oct 1707, announcing his arrival and reception by the Bishop, Chapter, Magistrato and the Operai della Madonna di S. Martino. f.189r: silversmith's account ('Adi 30 Sett. 1700' - probably 1707) for two gold crowns, large and small, 153.85 scudi, 'Servirono p le Sacre Immagini della Sma Vergine e Suo Bambino Gesu nella Città di Monte Pulciano'; sums repeated on f.188v; wrapper f.194v 'Conto 2 ... Gio: Giardini Oref.'. ff.190r-192r, 196r-197v and 198r-v: three copies of the 'Relatione del seguito nella venuta ... Can.co Gio. Andrea Ricci in Montepulciano per coronare la Bma Vergine detta di S. Martino esistente nella Chiesa Cattedrale' (arrival dates garbled by OCR: '16 Ott.e 1701', '26 7bre 1760' with margin 'd'an: 1760', '5 Ott.e 1707'; the coronation day 6 November is consistent in all copies and the title leaf f.193v gives 1707). Coronation at the Mass after Communion; an instrument of consignment of the two crowns was rogated by the chancellor of the episcopal curia (not present; f.193v margin '(non vi è l'origine)'). f.195v margin: 'lettera delle M. S. ... Andrea Ricci ...'. The third copy of the relazione breaks off at f.198v, the last page of the range. | Two copies of the relazione (ff. 196r–198v), 'Memorie dello Scoprimento e Culto' drawn from episcopal visitations of 1610/1612 (ff. 200r–200v, two copies; ends 'De Anno 1707 ... ipsa Sacra Imago una cum Imagine Infantis Jesu in ejus sinu sedentis corona aurea fuit solemni pompa coronata'), Ricci's covering letter of the day after the crowning (f. 201r, OCR date 'Montepulciano 7 9.bre 1701' / 'Montegranaro 9 8br 1701', i.e. 7 Nov 1707), a 'Decretum 30 Junii 1704' of which only the heading was transcribed (f. 201v) — taken here as the concession date, medium certainty — and two copies of the notarial instrument of consignment (ff. 202r–203v; notary Oliverius Antonius Vannutius, chancellor Vincentius Pallini/Lattini; authenticated by the vicar general 15/18 Nov 1707; margin: 'Instrum. Donationis ... Politiana die 5. [or 8.] 9bris 1707'). Coronation date: relazione says Ricci arrived 26 Sept (OCR '1760') / 5 Oct 1707 and the ceremony was 'il dì 6. Nov.'; letter 'Coronatione di ieri mattina' confirms 6 Nov 1707; the instrument's OCR 'die sexta Mens. Sept./Feb.' is presumably 'Novembris'. f. 204v margin: 'Altra lettera del d.º S.r Ab.e Ricci ... relat.e ... alla coronaz.ne' (text not transcribed). Isolated margin words 'Antonelli' (f. 199r) and 'loco detto Sevratto' (f. 204v) unexplained — the latter probably belongs to the following Tersatto dossier. f. 196r opens with the head of the relazione; whether earlier Montepulciano documents precede f. 196r cannot be seen from this range. The instrument also alludes to the Chapter having earlier crowned images 'in celeberrimo D. Blasii Templo' (S. Biagio, Montepulciano) — not documented in this range.

sources.rubric_latin: Instrumentum Donationis Duarum Coronæ aureæ, factæ Imagini B. M. V. miraculosæ ... in Sacro, et Reali Monasterio Montis Virginis maioris de Alvito, factæ in Actis Regiis Die 17. Maij 1712
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Three heavily garbled OCR passes of one Latin attestation by the archbishop of Benevento ('Athanasius Ursinus, S. Beneventanae Ecclesiae Archiepiscopus'; signature OCR 'J. d. B. Card. Spinus Archiepiscopus' — i.e. Cardinal Orsini, archbishop of Benevento 1686–1724, inferred), dated Benevento 9 Jan 1708, testifying to the antiquity and miracles of an image of the Virgin painted by St Luke: brought by Baldwin, Emperor of Constantinople; 'Catharina Balduini'; Frederick's army 'anno 1239 juxta Beneventanam'; 'Brundusium'; 'Civitate Abellina' (Avellino); 'Monte praefato adscendere'; 'Guilelmo Abbati'; 'Congregationis Montis Virginis' — legend elements pointing to the Madonna di Montevergine, but one pass places the image 'in Ecclesia S. Angeli ...' (S. Angelo a Cupolo?) and another 'Monialium Asceterii', so the church is not securely read. Margin 'Car. ly / januarij Co:nat.' (Coronat.?) and '2/3'. Attestation only: no decree, crowns, deputy or coronation date in this range; dossier presumably continues past f. 215r. Wrapper f. 214v 'Corone d'oro' (margin '514') may belong to this dossier. | Dossier contents: (a) attestations on the origin of the image by the Archbishop of Benevento (OCR 'Athanasius Ursinus' / 'Card. Spinus Archiepiscopus', i.e. Card. Orsini), dated 9 January 1708, margin 'Attestati circa l'origine della Madonna di Monte Vergine nella Diocesi di Benevento, o sia Provincia del 1708' and 'Monte Vergine a del 1708' (heavily garbled Latin, ff. 215r–218v); (b) conto of the silversmith Gio. Giardini for two crowns 'per mandare alla Chiesa detta di Monte uergine di Napoli', settled 23 May 1711, 295 scudi (ff. 216r–217v); (c) decree 12 July 1711 (Lib. Decr. XX f. 8v) suspending the coronation because the image already had a gold crown, remitting the question to the Nuncio (f. 219r); (d) notarial copy of the donation instrument by D. Thomas Cervanetta of Mercogliano, dated in the text 'Die Decimoquarto mensis Maij' 1712 (margin says 17 May 1712), incorporating the Chapter's commission letter of Rome 24 [April] 1712, the 'Ordo servandi in Tradendis Coronis Aureis', and the brief of Clement XI of 29 April 1712 granting a plenary indulgence (ff. 220r–223v); (e) relazione of Canon Howard's journey (25 April–21 May 1712), coronation performed after first Vespers of Pentecost, i.e. Saturday 14 May 1712 (heading 'alli 14. di Maggio 1712'), ff. 224r–229v, with a printed 'avviso' from Naples quoted; (f) letter of the Abbot General D. Vito Antonio Pastorale, Montevergine 15 May 1712, and minuta of the Chapter's reply 5 June (or Aug.) 1712 (ff. 230v–233v). No explicit concession date appears; the Chapter's letter says only 'havendo Noi già da molto tempo Decretata la Corona d'oro'. Margin at f. 223v reads 'Montis Virginis maioris de Alvito' (OCR; expected 'de Monte'). 'cap. 63. pag: 435.' (f. 229r) and 'Lib. III. de S. M. V. a pag. 25' (f. 230r) may be bibliographic rather than register references.

MDCCCXXVI, ab eiusdem Capituli delegato, Cardinali Ruffo Scilla, aurea corona decoratum fuit'. Ruffo Scilla acted as delegate of the Vatican Chapter, not as papal Legate. The decree begins on printed p. 498 (passage printed_page is 500, where the coronation is mentioned). act_date is the Congregation's session date (die iv Maii MDCCCCIX); Pius X signed the commission on 12 May 1909.

No date; the image is the one venerated in the church 'Gesù Vecchio' in Naples of which Baccher was rector. Passage printed_page 153; decree opens on p. 152.

sources.incipit_latin: Parthenopen urbem praeclaram augusta Virgo, singulari ducta studio amoris, elegisse videtur, ubi non solum unum, sed plura constitueret domicilia pietatis

sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, instrumentum donationis, lettera, other, supplica
sources.legate: Prospero Lambertini, canon of St Peter's, Archbishop of Theodosia (delegate), who by letter of 21 July 1724 subdelegated Francesco Maria Carafa, Bishop of Nola; the crowns were imposed by Card. (Francesco) Pignatelli, Archbishop of Naples
sources.deputy: Prospero Lambertini, canon of St Peter's, Archbishop of Theodosia (delegate), who by letter of 21 July 1724 subdelegated Francesco Maria Carafa, Bishop of Nola; the crowns were imposed by Card. (Francesco) Pignatelli, Archbishop of Naples
sources.rubric_latin: Memoriale dato da d. PP. Teatini di S. Paolo Magg.re di Napoli, che supplicano il R.mo Cap.lo p la Coronat.ne della Mad.na della Purità, che si venera nella loro Chiesa con una Let.ta del S.r Card. Pignatelli
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'ad formam semicirculi constructas et perforatas, unciarum novem, valoris ducatorum circiter ducentum'; Giardini's account 174:97 scudi. Petitioner: Clerici Regolari Teatini di S. Paolo Maggiore, Napoli (Provost D. Filippo Sifola, Vicar D. Casimiro Salmieri, and the fathers), supported by a letter of Card. Pignatelli. Supplica dated 'Napoli 4 di 9bre 1713' (= 4 Nov 1713); letter of Card. Pignatelli, Napoli 3 March 1714; letter of P. Savino, canon of St Peter's (undated); margin note reads 'Concesso 27 Marze 1700' — the year is OCR-suspect and 1714 is inferred from the surrounding dates, so concession_date is an inference. 'Other' = extract from Carlo Celano's Notizie di Napoli (1725) on S. Paolo Maggiore, the church of Suor Orsola Benincasa and S. Chiara (Giotto Madonna) — the latter two images are merely described, not crowned; also payment mandates to the silversmith Giacomo Antonio Giardini (30 scudi on 14 Jan 1717) and Giardini's account for the two crowns (174:97 scudi), which mislabels the church as 'S. Carlo de Padri Teatini'. Instrument (Latin, Naples, 7 Sept 1724, notary Thomas Cerillo, copy authenticated 1 Feb 1725) inserts Lambertini's letter of Roma 21 July 1724 ('corrente anno 1624' is OCR for 1724). Margin at f.300v labels it 'Instrumentum Coronationis Sae: Imaginis B. M. V. Laetitiae in Ecclesia Divi Pauli Maj. ... Neapoli factae die 7. Septembris 1724' ('Laetitiae' is probably an OCR/archivist slip for Puritatis). A further stray margin note at f.301r, 'Instrumentum Coronationis Sac: Imagini B.M.V. Luscintani', is unreadable and not tied to any document in the range.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA V., « DE PONTE » APPELLATA, PATRONA CAELESTIS AEQUE PRINCIPALIS CUM S. IUVENALE CIVITATIS AC DIOECESIS NARNIENSIS DECLARATUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Viam vitae insistentes Christifideles tot inter pericula et acerbitates, recto haud labuntur itinere et ad locum petitum, sempiternam dicimus beatitatem, feliciter perveniunt
sources.notes: Patron declaration; attests 'Simulacrum Almae Deiparae de Ponte ... a Carolo Maria Cardinali Sacripante, anno millesimo septingentesimo quinquagesimo quarto, auctoritate Petriani Canonicorum Collegii, est aureo diademate inter acclamantis populi vota redimitum' — crowned in 1754 by Cardinal Carlo Maria Sacripante on the authority of the Vatican Chapter. A commemorative liturgical feast on 5 May was afterwards instituted with the approval of Pius IX. The image (BVM holding the Divine Child) was found in 1714. Vernacular form 'Madonna del Ponte' rendered from the Latin 'de Ponte'. Act begins on printed page 758 (passage indexed at 759).

sources.citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 142r–159v
sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: instrumentum donationis, other, relazione, stampa
sources.legate: Alexander 'Cia- Siy Coccianus' Romanus (OCR-garbled surname), Referendary of both Signatures, canon of St Peter's, specially deputed by the Chapter
sources.deputy: Alexander 'Cia- Siy Coccianus' Romanus (OCR-garbled surname), Referendary of both Signatures, canon of St Peter's, specially deputed by the Chapter
sources.rubric_latin: dat, donat, et concedit Be- atissimæ Virgini nuncupat. S.ti Brijj huius Ill.mo Civitatis Urbevetanae ... Duas Coronas Aureas ... in antiquiss. et Insigni Ecclesia Cathedrali
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'Duas Coronas Aureas', weight 7½ oz and 2 denari of gold, 276 scudi 8 [baiocchi?] Roman money excluding the goldsmith's fee. Petitioner: City of Orvieto (Confaloniere e Conservatori / publico Consiglio) through Bishop Vincenzo de' Conti degli Atti; crowns received in the instrument by Giovanni Battista Gualterio, camerlengo of the Fabbrica of the Cathedral. Only the first two pages of the Latin donation instrument fall within this range (f.142r–v); it breaks off at 'coronata' and continues past the range. Coronation date is the date of the instrument (8 June 1704, Clement XI anno IV), which states the crowns were brought 'ad effectum coronandi' and that the images were 'postea coram eisdem ... coronata' — read as same-day crowning, not explicitly confirmed. Diocese inferred from 'Civitatis Urbevetanae' and the mention of its bishop. The deputy's surname is OCR-garbled ('Cia- Siy Coccianus'); the bishop is named only as 'R.mo D. Fabritio Ep.'. No concession decree or margin note is visible in this range. The image is apparently the Madonna venerated in the Cappella di S. Brizio of Orvieto Cathedral (the text says 'nuncupat. S.ti Brijj'); the Child is named ('illiusque D.ni Filij'). The margin note on f.122r mentioning an 'Ab.te d'Orvieto: Andrea Ricci' may relate to this dossier. | Instrument of donation dated 8 June 1704 (notary Carlo Fontana of Orvieto), witnesses Leone Albergio and Monaldo Aurelio; the printed Racconto (by canon Lattanzio Silvestrucci, Orvieto: Livio Tosini) confirms the crowning on 8 June 1704 during solemn Mass, with feasts 8-10 June; a sonnet to D. Annibale Albani at f.159v. Margin note at f.143v reads 'conceditur 16 Jul. 1896' — year clearly garbled by OCR (1696 or 1703 possible), so concession_date left null; the same note reads 'Instrum. donationis duarum Coronarum aurearum factae Imaginis miraculosae B. M. V. in Ecclesia ... Civitatis Urbevet. ... die 27. May 1704' (partly garbled). The image was formerly called 'Santa Maria prisca' and 'S. Maria della Stella'. The bishop's name is garbled as 'Fabritio Ep.' in the Latin instrument but given as Vincenzo de' Conti degli Atti in the Racconto.

sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, instrumentum donationis, lettera, relazione
sources.legate: Francesco Maria de Aste, Archbishop of Otranto, elected by the Chapter's letter of 10 Jan 1705 in place of one of its canons
sources.deputy: Francesco Maria de Aste, Archbishop of Otranto, elected by the Chapter's letter of 10 Jan 1705 in place of one of its canons
sources.rubric_latin: Instrum. Donationis Duar.m Coronar.m aurear.m fact simulacro miraculoso SS.mæ ... in Ecclesia Metropolitana Hydrunti Die 7 Maij 1705
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child), value 78 1/2 scudi d'oro in oro. Petitioner: Clero e Città d'Otranto; concession originally granted at the prayers of Card. de Aste (then a member of the Chapter). Concession date taken from the endorsement on f.82r ('Instrum Donationis duar Coronar aurear / concessio 14 Maii 1691', with silversmith Gio. Giardini's signature on f.82v); its attribution to Otranto is inferred (medium) from the 1705 letter stating the crown had been 'destinata' earlier at Card. de Aste's request and from the archbishop's information letter of 6/20 June 1691 (two copies, ff.83r-84r, endorsed 'Lettera di Mons. Arcivescovo d'Otranto in ordine alla Corona d'oro'). Instrument (two copies, ff.87r-88r) is dated 'Die vero Septima Martij' 1705, notary Angelo Stephanoch of Otranto; the archivist's endorsement reads '7 Maij 1705' but the archbishop's covering letter of 22 March 1705 (f.89r) confirms March. Conto on f.85r (Dom.co Vannini) for two crowns, 154:50 in all, sits inside this dossier and is presumed to belong to it. The 1691 letter records the statue's return from Valona (Vlorë) after the Turkish sack of 1480 and a jubilee granted by Pius V in 1564. Loose margin words 'Oronzo', '14', '85' on ff.85v-86v.

sources.rubric_latin: Relazione intorno all'Imagine della B. V. delle Grazie che si venera nella Chiesa Catted.le di S. Cristoforo della Città della Penna Residenza de' Vescovi di Montefeltro
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child), 65 scudi 1 denaro 21 grani of gold. Relazione (f. 104r-105v): image painted on the wall with the Child, altar consecrated 1215, lacrimation 20 March 1489, confraternity c. 1490 aggregated to the Gonfalone; 'coronata l'anno 1708 adì 15 Agosto' by Bishop Martorelli. Conto (f. 106r) dated 17 May 1705 for the two crowns, total 143:8 1/2, signed 'Tom.o Lannini Can.o Deput.o'; margin heading 'Relaz.e della B. V. nella Città di Penna, e Rieti' (Rieti unexplained). Latin instrument (f. 107r-107v) cites the Chapter's faculty 'Sub dat. Romæ 7 9mbris 1704' while the Chapter's Italian letter (f. 108r) is dated 'Roma 4. 9mbre 1707' (addressed 'Monsignor Corelli Vescovo di M.feltro', OCR for Martorelli) - year uncertain. The instrument's church reading 'Eccl.ia S.ti Arch.li Mich.is' conflicts with S. Christophori elsewhere and is probably OCR. Margin label f. 110v gives 'die 15. Aug.ti 1709' and the bishop's attestation 'Die 21 Augusti 1705' - both likely OCR/slips for 1708. The confraternity (Società della B. V. delle Grazie; deputies Gio. Carboni, Polidoro Valentini, Giuseppe Fabri) received the crowns and undertook the obligation. The cover f. 111v ('Decernitur Visitatio 10 Maii 1694 conceditur 11 Oct 1694') immediately follows this dossier but appears to belong to the unidentified 'Conto 2' at f. 112r; it may nevertheless be this image's concession.
