sources.rubric_latin: Desiderano i R. P. D. di cotesta Chiesa di S. Fiorenzo, che dal nostro Capitolo si adorni con la Corona d'oro la S. Imagine della SS.ma Vergine esistente nella loro Chiesa
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Petitioner: the Fathers (Religiosi) of the church of S. Fiorenzo, Perugia ('R. P. D. di cotesta Chiesa di S. Fiorenzo'); margin f.176r 'Servit...' suggests Servites. Letter of the Chapter (Rome, 31 July 1697, signed Aurelio Vittorio canon secretary) to a bishop ('Mons. Patritio Vescovo di ...', address on verso 'Colligio Sapienza / Perugia') asking for information on the antiquity, fame of miracles and prior crowning of the image before deciding. Locality Perugia inferred from the address on f.170v. No concession in this range; the dossier ends at the last page of the range so may continue past it. | f.170r-v: letter of the Vatican Chapter, Rome 31 July 1697, to the Bishop of Perugia asking for information on antiquity, miracles and whether the image was already crowned. f.171r-171v and f.172r-v: two historical accounts (miracle of the mason's apprentice Camillo Serafini who tried to cover the image with lime, 1617; episcopal process 'Madonne S. Florentij'; translation into the church 1646); the second ends 'Fu coronata questa l'anno 1720 ... Monsig. Ansildi ... Vescovo di Perugia ... il di 4 Novembre'. f.173r: silversmith's account dated 5 Ottobre 1726 for two gold crowns for the images in S. Fiorenzo, Perugia (265:30 scudi, mandate 162 scudi signed Gio. A. Ricci Segr.); f.174v wrapper 'Conto delle Corone d'Oro con Giacomo Ant. Giardini Argent.'. The OCR year '1720' conflicts with the 1726 account; 1726-11-04 adopted as the coronation date (crowns made Oct 1726), so the date is inferred - medium confidence. f.176v margin notes: 'Madonna indos[?]', 'Diocesi di Perugia', 'Dalla Cancellaria Vescovile', 'possa N. 93', 'Armario N. 63', 'Peruggia'. No concession decree or date seen in range.

sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Margin f. 100v: 'conceditur 28 9bris 1693' and 'consignatio ... Lib. XIX. f.º 387'. Giardini's account (f. 98r-98v) for two crowns for 'la SS.ma Madonna e Suo Bambino di S. Pantaleo in Roma', total 166:95, 100 scudi on account 19 Dec 1693. The coronation_date is the date of the Latin receipt (f. 99r, 'Die 25. Martij 1694') in which the Piarist Praepositus Generalis Jo. Franciscus a S. Petro acknowledges the two crowns (value 121:55) 'quae fuerunt collocatae per D. Joannem Giardinum aurificem super capitibus' - the ceremony itself is not otherwise described. The 'Breve relazione dell'origine' (f. 101r-101v) gives the image's history (painted by an anonymous Perugian painter, given by Aurora Berti to the Piarists); 'Insignificanz.a' in the margin is OCR.

Their authority ('autorizza'): Capitolo; their decree date 9-9-1647. Their annotazioni: Bombelli:la titola Santa Maria in Portico in Campitelli. Briccolani: la titola Santa Maria in Portico in Campitelli. Their note: Lamina di rame con smalti del XI secolo. La chiesa di Santa Maria in Portico in Campitelli indicava l'immagine della Madonna del portico che si trova nella chiesa in Campitelli. Al momento dell'incoronazione la chiesa si chiamava Santa Maria in Portico. Dopo la pestilenza del 1656, a causa dell'afflusso di fedeli ed essendo la chiesa troppo piccola, Papa Alessandro VII decise di ingrandire la chiesa Santa Maria in Campitelli dei chierici e il 14 gennaio 1662 vi fu traslata l'immagine di Santa Maria in Portico, insieme al titolo cardinalizio della chiesa. Nel 1662 la chiesa Santa Maria Portico cambiò titolo e divenne Santa Galla che fu demolita nell'anno 1930.

sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, decretum, lettera, other, supplica
register_refs: ex decr. caplanibus To. XVIII p. 13
ex libr. XVIII. Decr. Cap. p. 6
sources.rubric_latin: Decreta fuit 17. Xbris 1696 corona redimita in die Assumptionis 1697 ex decr. caplanibus To. XVIII p. 13.
sources.notes: Crowns: one new gold crown for the Child ('una Corona d'oro lavorata con fiori e cartelle per il Bambino'); the existing crowns of the Virgin and Child recoloured and burnished. Petitioner: Capitolo e Canonici della Basilica di S. Pietro (the Chapter itself). Contents: decree 2 March 1697 deputing the Sacrista Maggiore and Fabretti to oversee restoration of the sacristy chapel where the image stands (100 scudi from the Fabbrica); account of 25 June 1697 for the Child's crown (39.45 scudi, signed Tomaso Vannini camerlengo), docket 'Gio: Giardini Orefice'; supplica to the Pope for a plenary indulgence for the crowning 'alli 14 del corrente mese d'Agosto', granted 7 Aug 1697 by Card. Albani 'pro unica vice'; a note (f.168r, dated 3 Jan 1695 by 'Parruccini Vic.o') that Innocent XII conceded the indulgence for the crowning after the Vespers of the Assumption, with f.168v recording an indulgence brief of 11 Aug 1695 (Caps. 1 fasc. 2), suggesting the crowning was first planned for 1695 and carried out in 1697; f.169r gives the inscription on the Child's crown 'Cap.lum S. Petri de urbe hanc cor. au. ex legato Ill.mi Com. Alex. Sfortiae An. 1697'. Coronation date: docket says 'in die Assumptionis 1697', supplica says 14 August (eve/after Vespers) — 15 Aug 1697 adopted, 14 Aug possible. f.167r is a later letter to Mons. Guerrieri asking that the image, 'la prima ad esser decorata della corona d'oro' in Sforza's lifetime, be crowned anew. OCR gives 'Madonna della Pieve' at f.168r for 'della Febre'. | f.168r (OCR) calls the image 'Madonna s:ma della Pieve ... nella Sagrestia della Basilica di S. Pietro' - almost certainly 'della Febre' as f.169r reads. f.168r: letter of the Vicar (Parruccini Vic.o) on the plenary indulgence granted by Innocent XII for the day of the coronation, 'Dati li 3. Gen. 1695'; f.168v: note on the Brief 'Dat. 11. Aug. 1695 = Caps. 1. fasc. 2.' and 'Decreta fuit 17. Xbris 1696 corona redimita in die Assumptionis 1697 ex decr. caplanibus To. XVIII p. 13'; f.169r: text of the inscription on the crown ('Cap.lum S. Petri de urbe hanc cor. au. ex legato Ill.mi Com. Alex. Sfortiae An. 1697'). Years 1695 vs 1696/97 may be OCR noise. This is the first leaf of the range; earlier documents of this dossier may lie in the preceding batch (not visible).

sources.citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 90r–97v
sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, instrumentum donationis, relazione, stampa
sources.legate: Scipione de' Ricci, Patrizio Fiorentino, Referendary of both Signatures, Canon of St Peter's
sources.deputy: Scipione de' Ricci, Patrizio Fiorentino, Referendary of both Signatures, Canon of St Peter's
sources.rubric_latin: RELAZIONE DEL PRINCIPIO, E CAUSE DELLA VENERAZIONE DELL'IMMAGINE DELLA SANTISSIMA VERGINE DETTA DELLE GRAZIE DELLA TERRA DI S. GIOVANNI Da Coronarsi solennemente il dì 8. di Settembre 1704
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child), weight 59 scudi d'oro meno 9 grani per conto. Petitioner: Operai of the Oratory (Giovanni Michele Santini, Alessandro de' Bessi, Vittorio de' Rossi, Antonio Camillo de' Giovini, Andrea del Bello) / Deputati sopra la Solennità. Instrument (two copies, ff.91r-92r) actum 8 Sept 1704 at S. Giovanni under Cosimo III, notary Ottaviano de' Pasquini(?) da Lastra/Camerina; crowning performed in the Oratory at pontifical Mass of Orazio 'de Lanciarichis' (Panciatichi), Bishop of Fiesole. Concession date from endorsement f.92v.01 'Romæ sub die 15 maii 1704' (reading as the decree date is an inference, medium). Second endorsement f.92v.02 is badly garbled ('B. M. V. de Rupe, sive nuncupatæ Tra:tarn ... Actum die 27 Aug. 1707') — likely OCR damage on the same instrument, not a separate event. Register ref 'Caps. 39. fasc. 38g' probably = 'Caps. 39. fasc. 3'. Conto on f.90r names the image as 'esistente nella cità di Fiesole in Toschana' (i.e. diocese). f.93v: a mostly unread conto by 'Gio. Giustini/Giardini Argentiere' with margin 'conceditur die 6 Octobr' (no year) and '5 Octobr' on f.94r — placement suggests it belongs to this dossier but it could concern another image. Printed Relazione (Firenze, Michele Nestenus, 1704) ff.94r-97v narrates the 1479 miracle of Mona Tancia and the 1596 fire. | Tail end of a printed historical relazione (long-s typography) that begins in the previous batch; the page opens mid-text ('E Fabio Segni col seguente'). The image's title is not given in this range: it is described as the miraculous painted image of the Virgin and Child at the Porta di S. Lorenzo of the Terra of S. Giovanni in Tuscany / Valdarno ('Beatus Aegidius in Valle Arnensi in Tuscia'; Florentine dominion), with the 1479 Mona Tancia milk miracle, the 1596 fire, privileges of Sixtus IV and Innocent VIII. The relazione closes 'si porta da Noi Deputati sopra la mentovata Incoronazione', so a coronation had been performed, but no date, deputy or concession appears here. The modern designation (Madonna delle Grazie, San Giovanni Valdarno) is an inference, not in the text. Country inferred from Tuscany/Firenze.

sources.rubric_latin: Memoriae proditur Summum Pontificem Ioannem Paulum PP. sources.incipit_latin: Ubi victoria de malo subest et de peccato ipsaque de morte ea quidem est tribuenda Christi sacrificio, qui homo est factus.
sources.notes: The Pope crowned the image himself during Mass on his pastoral visit, at the request of Abp Settimio Todisco. Letters signed 'De speciali mandato Sanctissimi' by Abp Giovanni Battista Re, Substitute. Country not stated in the act; inferred from the Latin diocese/place name.

sources.notes: Basilica minor elevation act which states in passing that John Paul II himself crowned the image: 'ubi impensa pietate colitur imago Dei Genetricis « Nicopeia » nuncupatae, quam Nos Ipsi in Petriano huiusce almae Urbis foro anno MCMXCVI coronavimus'. Could equally be classed papal_personal_coronation, but the act's own object is the basilica title. Only the year (1996) of the crowning is given, in St Peter's Square. Country (Italy) inferred from San Vito dei Normanni / Brindisi-Ostuni, not stated. Act begins on printed page 346; passage printed_page was 345.

V. ab Arcu appellatae apud urbem Neapolim, primo volvente saeculo ex quo eadem Deiparae imago aureo diademate redimita fuit.
sources.incipit_latin: Quemadmodum accepimus, die VIII mensis Septembris hoc anno, quo saeculum implebitur ex quo Beatae Mariae Virginis imago, quae in aede, eidem Deiparae ab Arcu appellatae apud urbem Neapolim sacra, piis obsequiis colitur, aureo diademate fuit redimita, peculiaria sollemnia ibidem agentur.
sources.notes: Not a coronation act: the Pope sends a Missus Extraordinarius to preside at the centenary of the image's golden crowning. Coronation year derived from 'primo volvente saeculo' with the celebration on 8 September 1974, so the crowning was in 1874 (very likely 8 September 1874) - verify the exact day. Country Italy inferred from 'apud urbem Neapolim' (Naples); no diocese named in the act. Vernacular title rendered from the Latin 'ab Arcu appellatae'. The act also recalls that Pius IX visited the sanctuary and venerated the image. Confirmed by the volume indices at pp. 759, 788, 792. The sanctuary of the Madonna dell'Arco is at Sant'Anastasia.

sources.notes: Attests the personal coronation by Pius VII: 'eundemque anno post, aurea corona simulacro Savonensi imposita, votum Mariae Auxiliatrici christianorum solvisse' ('abhinc fere centum annis'). Year 1815 reconstructed (a year after Pius VII's return in 1814); not printed as a numeral. Benedict XV here deputes Andrea Card. Ferrari, Archbishop of Milan, as his Legate to the centenary solemnities - not to a coronation - so the legate field is left null. The letter begins on printed p. 201; the passage's printed_page is 202.

sources.act_type: Epistola

sources.notes: Letter for the fourth centenary of the 1536 apparition to Antonio Botta. Coronation recorded: 'simulacrum Virginis, ibidem religiose excultum, ab ipso Romano Pontifice corona est redimitum. Quod quidem contigit, quum Pius VII ... die x Maii anno MDCCCXV ...' and later 'dies x Maii, quo Virginis simulacro aurea corona per augustas manus imposita est'. D. 1938'.

sources.legate: Abbate Gio. Andrea Ricci, canon of the Vatican Basilica
sources.deputy: Abbate Gio. Andrea Ricci, canon of the Vatican Basilica
documents: other (attestation of the Vicar General Orazio Piccolomini Aragona, 9 June 1704)
sources.rubric_latin: Relatione del seguito nella uenuta dell'Illmo e Rmo Monsig.r Ricci à Siena à coronare la Bma Vergine del Presepio nella Chiesa delle Monache d'ogni Santi
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child), weight 'centum sexaginta'. Cover f. 113v: 'Visitatio Decernitur 11 Julii 1695', 'Decreverunt 29 Julii 1695' ('Gio: Gianlorenzi Ajo' unexplained). Printed pastoral letter of Archbishop Leonardo Marsili, Siena 31 May 1704 (f. 114r inserts; the 114v insert also carries an OCR-transcribed printed letter dated 1611 that seems unrelated). Letter of the archbishop to his brother Ab. Cervini on the image's history (statues delivered by an unknown youth in 1446, declared miraculous 1653 and 1667; f. 115r). Latin instrument of 7 June 1704, notary Simon Sciarelli, with the nuns' names (f. 116r-117r); margin label f. 117v with 'Cap. 39. fol. 329'. Ricci's letter to the Chapter, Siena 8 June 1704 (f. 118r) and relazione (f. 119r-120v): crowning on Saturday 7 June 1704 after Vespers. Discrepancies: heading f. 115v says 'coronata li 5 Giugno 1707' and the relazione once says 'Sabbato 2 Giugno' - both OCR/slips; 7 June 1704 is consistent throughout. The margin at f. 122r ('... Ab.te d'Orvieto: Andrea Ricci al R.mo Cap.lo') continues the label of Ricci's letter.

sources.citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 24r–69v
sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, decretum, instrumentum donationis, other, relazione, stampa, supplica
sources.legate: Camillo Mugiasca (Mugiacea), canon of the Vatican Basilica, 'ad haec specialiter deputatus'
sources.deputy: Camillo Mugiasca (Mugiacea), canon of the Vatican Basilica, 'ad haec specialiter deputatus'
sources.rubric_latin: I Deputati della Madonna ss.ma di Tirano in Valtellina Dioc. di Como ... / margin f.26v: '10 Apr. 1690 Decreta fuit'
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'duas Coronas Auri', 18 ounces, value 200 scudi auri de Camera (instrument); 'doi Corone di Oro ... de la Madonna e del suo Bambino' (silversmith's account). Petitioner: Deputati della Madonna SS.ma di Tirano (Deputati et Rectores of the sanctuary: Antonio Meriti, Orazio Francesco Lucino, Domenico Mattio, Giacomo Liazzi), through a supplica to Pope Alexander VIII; the commemorative inscription says the honour was procured by Francesco Saverio Guicciardi, Bishop of Narni. Only the undated petition to the Pope (f.24r-v) and an inserted printed sheet with Latin captions listing the Virgin's miracles ('Præsentissima Virginis Tiranensis ope', 'Vbi steterunt pedes Mariæ', 'cum privil.') fall within this range; no decree, instrument or coronation date is visible here. The dossier runs to the end of the batch (f.25v blank) and is shared with the next batch, so any concession/coronation documents would lie past this range. Image subject not specified in these pages (whether with Child unknown). 'Levmaria' in the OCR is unclear (perhaps 'Lombardia'/'Germania'). | Whole range is one dossier. Contents: supplica of the Deputati to Alexander VIII (ff.24r-24v, docket f.26v with margin note '10 Apr. 1690 Decreta fuit' = concession date); printed devotional sheets inserted at f.25r ('Praesentissima Virginis Tiranensis ope', 'Ubi steterunt pedes Mariae') and ff.36r-37v ('Raptus Angelorum', 'Virgo Tiranensis'; one sheet marked 'Rinouato dal Bianchi 1780', a later insertion); silversmith's account f.27r (two gold crowns for Madonna and Bambino, total 239.20 scudi after tare; silversmith named in margin f.32v as 'Gio: Giardini Arg.o'; ff.31r-32v otherwise only page numerals); notarial instrument ff.28r-30r drawn by Paolo Francesco Bononi, notary of Como, dated Friday 29 Sept 1690 (weekday verified), crowns placed on the heads of the images of the Virgin and Child in the church, hymn Ave Maris Stella sung; vicar-general's attestation dated Como 7 Oct 1690; authenticated copy (f.33r) of the inscription on a large commemorative 'Quadro' hung in the sanctuary, signed by canon G. B. Robustelli; Mugiasca's relazione ff.34r-35r (left Como 1 Sept 1690, crowning on the feast of St Michael with ~20,000 people, Mass sung by the archpriest, Capuchin panegyric); f.35v is a stray unrelated fragment of Chapter business; ff.38r-48v a printed book 'Breve Istoria della miracolosissima Madonna di Tirano' by Gio. Antonio Cornacchi (1621; reprint Parma/Milano 1747), which runs on past f.48v. The place is called 'Tivano' in parts of the instrument (OCR/scribal variant of Tirano). The relazione (f.34v) has the panegyric 'in Lode della Beata Vergine del Lago' — likely OCR garbling, since every other document names Tirano. The instrument locates Tirano in the 'Statuum Ill.mor D.norum Rhetorum' (under the Grisons in 1690); country given as Italy on the basis of the place itself (the supplica calls it 'uno dei più famosi Santuarii d'Italia'). The crowned object is described as 'la Statua in mezzo la Chiesa' in the relazione, while the book describes the altar ancona with the effigy of Our Lady standing; the instrument speaks of two 'Sacrae Imagines' (Virgin and Child). No 'Lib.'/'Caps.' register cross-references occur in this range; the marginal numerals (30-46) are foliation/page counts only. Supplica begins with its heading at f.24r, so the dossier appears to start here, but folios before 24r were not visible. | Only a printed booklet (chapters IV to the end, with 'Addizioni', twelve Latin 'Elogia' on the Venerable Mario Omodei, and a closing protestation signed 'Homodaeus Anonymus') is in range; it begins mid-way (printed p. 45 at f. 46r), so chapters I-III and any supplica/decree/instrument for this image lie before pb 113. No coronation document, concession date or deputy is visible in the range. Diocese taken from the booklet itself ('Archivio del Vescovato di Como', 'Vescovo di Como'). Which image was crowned (the 'Ancona ... con l'effigie di Nostra Signora Santissima in piedi' over the privileged altar, or the facade statue with the Child) is not stated. OCR damage: many pages have marginal columns of broken word-fragments (pb 115, 117, 124-125, 129, 131, 133, 135, 137, 141, 143, 145, 147, 149, 151, 153).

legates: Augustinus S. R. E. Presbyter Cardinalis Richelmy, Archiepiscopus Taurinensis

sources.act_type: Breve
sources.legate: Augustinus S. R. E. Presbyter Cardinalis Richelmy, Archiepiscopus Taurinensis
sources.rubric_latin: BREVE quo Archiepiscopo Taurinensi committitur facultas solemniter coronandi, nomine et auctoritate Apostolica, Imaginem Mariae SS. Auxiliatricis.
sources.incipit_latin: Omnium sane templorum quae bo. me. Ioannes Bosco Salesianae Sodalitatis pater legifer ad maiorem Dei gloriam
sources.notes: Rubric OCR reads 'nomine et tauctoritate Apostolica' -> 'auctoritate'; addressee line OCR spaced as 'R i c h e l m y'. The Brief commits to the Archbishop of Turin the faculty to crown the image 'solemni ritu Nostro nomine et auctoritate', with a diadem to be imposed on both heads ('sacro utrique capiti tum Virginis tum Pueri Iesu diadema pro dignitate imponatur') - so the Infant Jesus is crowned as well. Petitioner: Michael Rua, Rector Major of the Salesians. Classified as papal_coronation_act because this is the granting act itself, though it simultaneously deputes Card. Richelmy to crown in the Pope's name (papal_legate_deputation is a defensible alternative). Exact coronation date not stated: only 'huius anni die per te eligendo', i.e. a day of 1903 to be chosen by the Archbishop. Datum 'die XIII Februarii MCMIII' = 1903, the second year of ASS vol. 35 (1902-03). Text of the act runs on to printed p. 581.

sources.act_type: Epistola
sources.rubric_latin: EPISTOLA SS.mi D. N. Leonis PP. XIII ad Moderatorem Generalem Salesianorum, occasione eorumdem conventus.
sources.incipit_latin: Cogendum proxime significabas Salesianorum ex omni terrarum orbe conventum, eumque, Deiparae Adiutricis ope suffultum
sources.notes: Incidental mention inside a letter to Michael Rua: the forthcoming international Salesian congress is to close with the solemn crowning of the image - 'solemniis iri conclusum declarabas eiusdem magnae Dei Matris insigni corona induendae'. Same image as ASS 35, 580 (Maria Auxiliatrix, Turin); dedup expected. The letter itself names no church or town, but the address line reads 'Dilecto filio Michaeli Rua Moderatori Generali Sodalitatis Salesianae Augustae Taurinorum', hence Turin; locality/diocese/country inferred from that address line, so confidence lowered to medium. Datum OCR 'die x n Maii MGMIII' read as die XII Maii MCMIII = 1903-05-12 (Pontificatus anno vigesimo sexto confirms 1903). Coronation year 1903 inferred from the imminence of the congress relative to the letter's date.

images.image_title_latin: Imago miraculosa B. M. Virginis Lauretanae Ven. Ecclesiae S. Nicolai a Clara RR. PP. Clericorum Regularium Congregationis Teatinorum Veronae
images.church_or_sanctuary: Santa Casa / Santuario della B. Vergine di Loreto contiguous to the Chiesa della Giara of the Chierici Regolari (Teatini); coronation performed in the Chiesa di S. Nicolò dei Teatini
legates: Gio. Francesco Barbarigo, Bishop of Verona (margin note: '30 9bris 1708 R. D. Barbarigo ad imponend. coronam deputatus')

sources.citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 235r–241v
sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, instrumentum donationis, other, relazione, stampa
sources.legate: Gio. Francesco Barbarigo, Bishop of Verona (margin note: '30 9bris 1708 R. D. Barbarigo ad imponend. coronam deputatus')
sources.deputy: Gio. Francesco Barbarigo, Bishop of Verona (margin note: '30 9bris 1708 R. D. Barbarigo ad imponend. coronam deputatus')
sources.rubric_latin: Breue notizia dell' Incoronazione della B. Vergine della Giara, da farſi nella Chieſa di S. Nicolò d[e' Chierici Regolari] ... Verona li 3. Nou. 1709
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Petitioner: PP. Chierici Regolari Teatini of the Giara, Verona ('porgere umile istanza all'istesso Reverendissimo Capitolo di S. Pietro'). Contents: (a) conto of the silversmith (f. 235r; signed 'Gio: Giardini Arg.ro' on the wrapper f. 238v) for two crowns 'all'Imperiale' of 15 December [1708] 'p.a La Madonna di Loreto e Bambino da PP. Teatini della Ghiara di Verona', 166 sc. 97½, final payment ordered 17 May 1709; (b) notarial act by Bernardo Ronchi, episcopal vice-chancellor, of the coronation performed in S. Nicolò by Bishop Barbarigo as delegate of the Chapter 'ex Epistola sub Dat. Romae die prima 8bris 1708', with chancery authentication (two copies, ff. 236r–237v; one copy's authentication reads 11 Aug. 1709, the other 11 9bris 1709); (c) printed 'Breve notizia' of the coronation, Verona 3 Nov. 1709 (ff. 239r, two OCR passes, text cut off at end of range). Coronation date: the OCR reads 'Die vero Dominica 19.a M[ensis] 8bris' 1709, but 19 Oct. 1709 was a Saturday, the stampa of 3 Nov. 1709 still calls the coronation 'da farsi', and the authentication is dated 11 Nov.; Sunday 10 Nov. 1709 fits all of these, so 1709-11-10 is a reconstruction (hence confidence medium; year 1709 is certain). Concession year 1708 inferred from the delegation letter of 1 Oct. 1708 and the margin note '30 9bris 1708 R. D. Barbarigo ad imponend. coronam deputatus' (f. 238v); no decree text is present. Crowns weighed 'Unciarum septem, unius quarti, et denariorum septem cum dimidio'. The Theatine provost was P. Pietro Paolo Masperoni. | Range opens mid-document: the closing formulae of the notarial act (notary Bernardo Ronchi, 'Veronae in Templo S. Nicolai Congregationis RR. PP. Teatinorum'), with episcopal authentication dated 11 Aug/11 Nov 1709 (OCR variants). Documents in range: notarial act close (237v inserts), Giardini's 'Conto 2 ... delle Corone d'Oro' cover with deputation note 30 Nov 1708 (238v), printed 'Breue notizia' (Verona, Fratelli Merli 1709; several copies, 239r-239v inserts), archivist label 'Relazione del origin. e promozione ... nella Chiesa de RR Teatini di Verona 1709' (239v.05), and printed programme 'Il Trionfo di Maria' fireworks for the coronation of the 'Madonna della Chiesa della Giara delli Chierici Regolari in Verona' dedicated to Bishop Barbarigo (240r-241v). The image is a statue of the Madonna of Loreto with Child made in Loreto and installed 25 Mar 1648. The programme says the bishop was deputed 'fin da principio' to avoid sending a Roman prelate; one garbled OCR copy (pb 567) mentions 'Monsignor Marchese Casali Canonico' as deputed, but this passage does not appear in the other copies and looks like OCR confabulation. Concession date not given in range (only the deputation date 30 Nov 1708).

sources.rubric_latin: Unicae Et Vetustissimae Viterbiensium Spei Ac Liberatrici Deiparae Mariae Virgini In Hac Vera Archetypi Sui Vultus Imagine Non Sine Prodigio Depictae
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'due Corone d'oro, una grande, et una piccola', made by Giovanni Giardini, argentiere, Rome, total 169.76½ scudi. Petitioner: Città / Magistrato di Viterbo (Comunità di Viterbo; letter of Bernardino Baroni, 25 May 1712). Letter of Bernardino Baroni (margin: 'Belardino Peroni', secretary of the Comunità di Viterbo), Viterbo 25 May 1712, about the city's failed plans to fund a solemn coronation and leaving it to the friars. Margin f. 123v labels it as concerning 'la Madonna S.ma della Quercia' - contradicting the letter's 'della Trinità' and f. 124r's 'Chiesa de Padri Agostiniani della Città di Viterbo'; probably an archivist's slip or OCR. Margin f. 123v: 'Decrevere 28 Maii 1696'. f. 124r: payment order of 27 Sept 1715 signed 'Moreno Vaiani Econ.o Dep.to'. No relazione or instrument in range and f. 124v is the last page, so the dossier likely continues. | The letter on f.122r (Bernardino Baroni, Viterbo 25 May 1712) opens mid-text with no salutation, so the dossier probably begins on the preceding leaf (outside this range). Concession date taken from the margin note 'Decrevere 28 Maii 1696' on f.123v; the same note reads the image as 'Madonna S.ma della Quercia' (OCR) whereas the letter itself and all other documents say 'della Trinità' / 'Liberatrice' — treat 'Quercia' as an OCR or archivist slip. The Latin instrument on f.128r reads 'die duodecima Mensis Iulii' (OCR), but the Breve Notizia, the pastoral letter, the inscriptions ('Idibus Novembris') and the archivist's note all give 12 November 1715. The pastoral letter (Card. Michelangelo Conti, bishop of Viterbo e Toscanella, Rome 1 Nov 1715, printed Viterbo 1715) and the Breve Notizia both survive in two copies (ff.127r, 130r–136r). Margin note on f.122r 'Sacra mad.na dal R.m... Ab.te d'Orvieto: Andrea Ricci al R.mo Cap.lo di S. Pietro' is obscure and may belong to another letter. f.136v.02 (pb 328) carries a stray list of Genoese-looking names (Martinengo, Giustiniani, Manganaro) with a marginal '181', unrelated to the coronation. The silversmith's account is dated 28 Sept / 9 Nov 1715; the first payment order is dated 27 Sept 1715 (Moreno Vaiani, Economo Deputato). | Only the last leaf of a dossier: a transcription of a votive inscription set up by S.P.Q.V. (Viterbo) on the Nones of May 1703 (Clement XI) thanking the Virgin for preserving the city from the earthquakes of that year; placed 'a parte Epistolae Maioris Altaris' (church not named). Copied 3 Oct 1856 by Alessandro D'Achille. f.140v-141r blank. No coronation data visible in this range; the dossier proper must precede f.140r.

Their authority ('autorizza'): Capitolo; officiated by Parroco don Carlo Occhipinti, delegato dal vescovo; their decree date 30-6-1784. Their annotazioni: ERR - Briccolani: data l'incoronazione 1785. Their note: La statuetta lignea, copia dell’antico simulacro custodito a Loreto, proviene dal Santuario lauretano. Fu portata da Fra’ Fedele da Vittoria, un terziario cappuccino devoto alla Madonna, il quale la ricevette in dono mentre si trovava in pellegrinaggio nel 1740. Le corone furono realizzate a spese della città dall’orafo del Capitolo di San Pietro, Bartolomeo Boroni. Questa chiesa apparteneva ai PP Cappuccini fino al 1992, ma in seguito alla soppressione degli Ordini Monastici (1866) non appartenne più a loro. Venne infine loro affidata dal Fondo per il Culto e successivamente dalla Diocesi. Incoronò il parroco locale, su delega del vescovo, a sua volta delegato dal Capitolo Vaticano. All'epoca dell'incoronazione, Vittoria apparteneva alla provincia di Siracusa e tale rimase fino all'anno 1927.

sources.legate: Dominicus Card. Ferrata
sources.rubric_latin: AD V. E. DOMINICUM CARD. FERRATA, ARCHIPRESBYTERUM LATERANENSEM, QUEM RENUNTIAT LEGATUM SUUM AD CONVENTUM EUCHARISTICUM MELITENSEM.
sources.incipit_latin: Inter publicas illustrioresque significationes Fidei, quas hoc anno per saecularia Constantiniana daturum est catholicum nomen
sources.notes: Letter naming Ferrata Legate to the Malta Eucharistic Congress; it recalls in passing that Pius X had earlier sent him to Malta to crown a Marian image: 'ea ipsa loca non ita pridem, missus item a Nobis, adivisti, ut sacerrimo Virginis Deiparae simulacro quod Conspicuae colitur, auream coronam imponeres'. 'Conspicuae' is a locative and is read as Cospicua (Bormla), Malta - identification inferred, hence medium confidence. No date is given for the crowning ('non ita pridem'). The diocese (Melitensis) is inferred from the Maltese setting, not stated for the image.

sources.rubric_latin: EMUS P. D. ALEXIUS HENRICUS M. TIT. SANCTAE SUSANNAE S. R. E. PRESB. CARDINALIS LÉPICIER DEPUTATUR AD AUREA CORONA ORNANDUM SIMULACRUM B. MARIAE V. « TA PINU » NUNCUPATAE IN EIUSDEM BASILICA DIOECESIS GAUDISIENSIS.
sources.incipit_latin: Marianum exstat Sanctuarium insigne Gaudisiensis dioecesis intra fines, quod iam Basilicae Minoris titulo privilegiisque Nos ipsi Litteris Apostolicis Nostris
sources.notes: Cardinal Lépicier, already Legate to the Regional Council of Malta, is charged 'ut arbitrio eius eligendo die ... aureum diadema Nostro nomine et auctoritate imponat' — day left to the legate, so no coronation date. The painting is described as by Stephanus Amedeus de Perusia, 1619. The act itself recalls that the sanctuary was made a minor basilica by Litterae Apostolicae of 31 Aug. 1932. No town named (the shrine is at Għarb); country inferred from the diocese of Gozo and the reference to the neighbouring diocese of Malta. The sanctuary of Ta' Pinu is at Għarb, Gozo.

sources.citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 75r–76v
sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: other, supplica
sources.rubric_latin: concedere La Corona alla Madonna S.ma delle Gratie in Malta esistente nello Chiesa Parochiale della Terra Zabar
sources.notes: Crowns: one requested ('concedere La Corona'). Petitioner: Francesco Pace, Maltese priest ('Fran.co Pace Sacerdote Maltese'), recommended by the Auditor Acquaviva ('raccommandato dall'Aud.re Acquaviva'). PETITION NOT CONCEDED — the image was not crowned. The Chapter's later docket on this dossier reads 'non si trova concessa' (Balzamo 2023, p. 189, citing BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, 4, f. 75r). Undated supplica; it cites as witnesses to the image's veneration the former Inquisitors and Apostolic Ministers of Malta: Cardinals Marescotti, Acquaviva, Ruffo, Pallavicino, and Mons. Passionei, Spinola, Caracciolo. ff. 75v-76r are blank; f. 76v is the docket ('Per Il Sacerdote Fran.co Pace Maltese p.r l'incoronatione di Una Madonna Miracolosa'). The range ends here, so any decree, instrument or relazione for Żabbar would lie beyond f. 76v and is not visible. | Petition only. Archivist's docket on f.76v: 'Per Il Sacerdote Fran.co Pace Maltese p.r l'incoronatione di Una Madonna Miracolosa — Non si trova concessa' (no concession found). Supplica cites Cardinals Marescotti, Acquaviva, Russo, Pallavicino and Mons. Passionei, Spinola, Caracciolo as former Inquisitors who venerated the image. 'other' = the archivist's docket note.

sources.act_type: Epistula
sources.rubric_latin: AD EMUM P. D. RODRIGUUM S. R. E. CARD. VILLENEUVE, ARCHIEPISCOPUM QUEBECENSEM, QUEM LEGATUM MITTIT AD CONVENTUM MARIALEM AD SANCTUARIUM B. MARIAE VIRGINIS GUADALUPENSIS MEXICOPOLI CELEBRANDUM.
sources.incipit_latin: Mater spei et gratiae Deipara Virgo cum ubique terrarum sacraria, ubi perpeti benignitate filiis alumnisque suis cuiuslibet generis solamina largitur
sources.notes: Letter deputing Card. Villeneuve as Legate to the Marian Congress (NOT to a coronation); it attests the earlier coronation in passing: 'cum quinquagesimus feliciter plenus annus decurrat, ex quo B. Virginis Mariae effigies aureo serto redimita est'. Coronation year 1895 is computed from the fiftieth year running in 1945, not stated verbatim; day/month not given. Legate field left null because the deputation is for the congress, not the crowning. Passage printed_page 255; letter opens on p. 254.

sources.act_type: Nuntius radiophonicus
sources.rubric_latin: CHRISTIFIDELIBUS DATUS DIE XII MENSIS OCTOBRIS A. MCMXLV, OB MARIALEM CONVENTUM AD SANCTUARIUM B. MARIAE V. GUADALUPENSI MEXICOPOLI COADUNATIS
sources.incipit_latin: Venerables Hermanos y amados hijos que, reunidos en torno a la persona de Nuestro dignisimo Cardenal Legado, conmemorais los cincuenta anos de la coronacion canonica de la Virgen de Guadalupe
sources.notes: Radio message for the Marian congress marking the fiftieth anniversary of the canonical coronation of the Virgin of Guadalupe: 'conmemorais los cincuenta anos de la coronacion canonica de la Virgen de Guadalupe' and 'Hace hoy cincuenta anos ... cuando sobre aquella frente angelical resplandecio la aurea corona'. Coronation date derived from 'today fifty years ago' relative to the act date 12 October 1945. Body is in Spanish, so incipit_latin holds the Spanish opening verbatim (accents lost in OCR). The Cardinal Legate is not named in the text. The act begins on this page (264); the same act continues to p. 267, where a further papal act is recorded separately.

sources.act_type: Nuntius radiophonicus
sources.rubric_latin: CHRISTIFIDELIBUS DATUS DIE XII MENSIS OCTOBRIS A. MCMXLV, OB MARIALEM CONVENTUM AD SANCTUARIUM B. MARIAE V. GUADALUPENSI MEXICOPOLI COADUNATIS
sources.notes: Same act as AAS-37-1945-ocr#g264 (act begins on p. 264; this passage carries pp. 266-268). Pius XII, speaking in the first person to the congress gathered round his Cardinal Legate, says: 'Nos, a quien la admirable disposicion de la Divina Providencia confio ... el sagrado tesoro de la divina sabiduria en la tierra ... Nos colocamos hoy de nuevo sobre tus sienes la corona, que pone para siempre bajo tu poderoso patrocinio la pureza y la integridad de la santa fe en Mejico y en todo el continente americano'. This is a re-crowning (a new crown placed 'de nuevo') declared by the Pope by radio while an unnamed Cardinal Legate presided in person, not a first canonical coronation and not a coronation performed by the Pope's own hand; classified papal_personal_coronation because the Pope himself states he places the crown. The source never uses a word for 'image', naming only the devotional title.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.rubric_latin: Rosa Aurea Basilicae Beatae Mariae Virginis a Guadalupe, intra fines archidioecesis Mexicanae positae, tribuitur asservanda.
sources.incipit_latin: Flores edens et spargens, sive olim, uti ferunt, cum prodigialem praesentiam suam testatam voluit, sive continenter, cum caelestia munera ... supplicibus dilargitur
sources.notes: Golden Rose act; coronation attested in passing: 'Leonem Pp. XIII concessisse, ut venusta imago, qua Deipara, appellatione illa insignis, exprimitur, suo nomine et auctoritate aureo diademate redimiretur'. Year of the coronation not given here (see AAS 62 (1970) 681, 75th anniversary in 1970). Address form: 'Venerabili Fratri Michaeli Dario Miranda et Gómez, Archiepiscopo Mexicano'; the Golden Rose was to be delivered by Card. Carlo Confalonieri (bearer, not a coronation legate).

sources.act_type: Nuntius radiotelevisificus
sources.rubric_latin: Universis Mexicanae Nationis christifidelibus, septuagesimo quinto exacto anno ex quo imago B. Mariae Virginis a Guadalupe aureo diademate redimita est.
sources.notes: Radio-television message of Paul VI for the 75th anniversary of the crowning of Our Lady of Guadalupe; the message body is in Spanish ('En el setenta y cinco aniversario de la Coronación de Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe...'), hence incipit_latin is null. Coronation year 1895 computed from the rubric ('septuagesimo quinto exacto anno') and the message date 12 October 1970 - not stated as such in the text; verify. The same event is listed in the volume indexes at pp. 876-877 and 911.

sources.act_type: Homilia (Iter Apostolicum in Mexicum)
sources.rubric_latin: Mane diei 27 m. ianuarii, Polonorum civium coloniam in Mexico degentium coram admisit, antequam e Delegationis Apostolicae aedibus templum B. M. V. a Guadalupe peteret. ... Inde profectus, ad sacram aedem pervenit, sacris litaturus atque Plenario Coetui Episcoporum Latinorum Americanorum, intercedente Beatissima Dei Genetrice, initium daturus. Quae inter sacra, hanc homiliam habuit
sources.notes: Found by extending the search over the surrounding pages of the same journey, as instructed; this page is NOT one of the 26 passages of batch G07 (the id follows the batch id convention for AAS-71-1979-ocr, page 177). Homily/prayer of John Paul II at the shrine of Guadalupe, 27 January 1979, at the Mass opening the III General Conference of the Latin American Episcopate. Spanish sentence, verbatim: 'Finalmente, oh Madre, recordando y confirmando el gesto de mis Predecesores Benedicto XIV y Pío X, quienes Te proclamaron Patrona de México y de toda la América Latina, Te presento una diadema en nombre de todos tus hijos mexicanos y latinoamericanos, para que los conserves bajo tu protección, guardes su concordia en la fe y su fidelidad a Cristo, Tu Hijo.' Same pattern as the Altagracia passage: the Pope presents a diadem to a devotion named by title; no formal coronation rite is described, and the words are addressed to the Virgin, not to an image (the image is mentioned separately on p. 175: 'Tu imagen en el Santuario de Guadalupe'). The homily begins on printed page 171; the diadem sentence is on p. 177. Locality 'Mexico City' is inferred — AAS names only the 'Santuario de Guadalupe' / 'templum B. M. V. a Guadalupe' in Mexico (Tepeyac is named on p. 173) — hence medium confidence. Body is in Spanish, so no Latin incipit; rubric_latin is the Latin editorial narrative of p. 171 (ellipsis marks omitted text).

Fu lì che l'immagine subì ustioni all'alluce del piede destro.

sources.act_type: Nuntius radiophonicus
sources.rubric_latin: NUNTIUS RADIOPHONICUS A BEATISSIMO PATRE, DIE XXXI MENSIS OCTOBRIS ANNO MCMXXXXIII, IN FESTO D. N. IESU CHRISTI REGIS, CHRISTIFIDELIBUS DATUS, OB III CONVENTUM EUCHARISTICUM E TOTA PERUVIANA NATIONE IN URBE TRUXILLENSI COADUNATIS
sources.notes: Radio message of Pius XII closing the 3rd Peruvian National Eucharistic Congress at Trujillo. Spanish original, p. 356: 'para que Tu, Virgen de la Puerta, solemnemente coronada el pasado miercoles'; Italian version, p. 359 (this passage): 'Tu, Vergine della Puerta, incoronata solennemente lo scorso mercoledi'. The source names only the devotional title, never an image, and does not state under whose authority the crowning took place; it is the Pope himself who acknowledges it, and the Congress was presided by his Legate. The act begins on p. 353 (Spanish) with the Italian version beginning p. 357; the rubric above is transcribed from p. 353, not from this passage. 'Last Wednesday' relative to the stated act date (31 October 1943, a Sunday) would be 27 October 1943, but the passage does not give a date, so only the year is recorded. Also greeted in the same sentence is 'Nuestra Senora del Socorro' of Huanchaco, of whom no crowning is said.

sources.notes: The letter lists among the fourth-centenary celebrations at Cebu 'Eucharisticus e tota Natione Conventus et coronatio statuae Iesu Infantis, in anteriore quadam expeditione eum in locum allatae', and deputes Card. Sanctuary not named (the Augustinian church at Cebu is implied by 'sacram aedem, quasi matricem ceterarum'). Archbishop of Cebu named: Iulius Rosales. Vernacular title (Santo Niño) not in the text.

sources.notes: Basilica Minor elevation stating 'Nostra demum aetate, Pii Pp. XI permissu ... imago, quam diximus, aureo diademate est redimita'. No year given; only that it was by permission of Pius XI (1922-1939). The act also recalls King John Sobieski praying before the image on his way to Vienna. The crowning is dated by Basilici–Bigliazzi 2025 (scheda 1121, following Anselmo 1933, who for post-1905 crownings worked from the Chapter's registers) to 15 August 1925: by papal brief, with crowns given and blessed by Pius XI, the rite performed by the Apostolic Nuncio Lorenzo Lauri; Anselmo has 21 December 1924 (the brief?) and 'solen. 6-I-925'. They record no other crowning at Piekary. This is the one event that AAS 55 (1963), 225 and AAS 111 (2019), 1343 both recite, so the two acts are held to one image (issue #1); the date is not entered in coronation_date because neither act states it and Basilici–Bigliazzi is not read as a source.

sources.notes: Listed by Basilici–Bigliazzi 2025 (scheda 532, their id 718), a modern compilation from Anselmo da Reno Centese 1933, the printed repertories and the internet, citing no folio; not read at first hand. Their authority ('autorizza'): B.P.; officiated by Monsignor Ludwik Jacobini, nunzio apostolico a Vienna, legato di papa Pio IX; their decree date #-#-1877. Their annotazioni: ERR - Frate Anselmo: la colloca a Starowics e la titola Santa Maria dei Morenti o Moribondi. Their note: Dipinto del XV secolo. Il dipinto rappresenta due scene; nella parte inferiore "La Dormizione di Maria", incoronata nel 1877 e nella parte superiore "Cristo che accoglie la Madre di Dio in cielo" incoronato nel 1899. Nel 1968 il dipinto fu bruciato con il Napalm dagli agenti dell'Ufficio Sicurezza, nel 2006 l'Istituto della Memoria Nazionale classificò l'evento come crimine comunista. Attualmente è esposta una copia del 1968, opera di Maria Niedzielska, che fu incoronata, con l'autorizzazione della Santa Sede, il 10 settembre 1972 dal Cardinale Stefan Wysznski Primate della Polonia la parte inferiore, e Monsignore Ignacy Tokarczuk arcivescovo di Przemysl la parte superiore.

sources.rubric_latin: Cestochoviae, occasione oblata coronationis quattuor Imaginum Beatae Mariae Virginis.
sources.notes: One of four images crowned personally by John Paul II at Jasna Góra, Częstochowa, on 19 June 1983 ('obrazie z sanktuarium w Stoczku, Diecezji Warmińskiej'). sources.act_type: Epistula (Legate deputation)
sources.rubric_latin: AD EMUM P. D. EMMANUELEM TIT. SANCTORUM MARCELLINI ET PETRI S. R. E. PRESB. CARDINALEM GONÇALVES CEREJEIRA, PATRIARCHAM LISBONENSEM, QUEM LEGATUM DELIGIT AD CONGRESSUM MARIALEM E TOTA LUSITANIA, AUGUSTAE BRACARUM AD SANCTUARIUM « MONTE DO SAMEIRO » CELEBRANDUM.

sources.act_type: Nuntius radiophonicus
sources.rubric_latin: NUNTIUS RADIOPHONICUS A BEATISSIMO PATRE, DIE XIII MENSIS MAII A. MCMXLVI, LUSITANIAE CHRISTIFIDELIBUS DATUS, SOLLEMNIA CELEBRANTIBUS AD SANCTUARIUM B. MARIAE V. A FATIMA, AUREA CORONA NOMINE SUMMI PONTIFICIS REDIMITAE.
sources.notes: Assigned passage is the volume index (printed p. 461); the document itself is the radio message at printed p. 264, used as aas_page. Body is Portuguese: 'por mäo do Nosso Cardeal Legado, acabamos de coroar a Imagem taumaturga' — the Pope crowned the image through an unnamed Cardinal Legate, so legate left null. Country explicit ('Lusitaniae christifidelibus'). Classified retrospective_attestation because the document is a homiletic radio message attesting the coronation just performed, not the deputation act itself.

sources.act_type: Epistula
sources.legate: Benedictus S. R. E. Cardinalis Aloisi Masella
sources.rubric_latin: AD EMUM P. D. BENEDICTUM TIT. SANCTAE MARIAE IN VALLICELLA S. R. E. PRESBYTERUM CARDINALEM ALOISI MASELLA, QUEM LEGATUM MITTIT AD CORONAM APPONENDAM SIMULACRO B. MARIAE V. DE FATIMA.
sources.incipit_latin: Celeberrima sollemnia, quae abhinc annos quattuor flagrantissima animorum pietate in honorem Beatae Mariae Virginis de Fatima a Lusitaniae fidelibus peracta sunt
sources.notes: Reached from the back-of-volume index passage (p. 494: 'Coronatio: ... simulacri B. Mariae V. de Fatima, 267, 376'); the act itself is the Epistula on p. 376: 'perinsignem imaginem Nostrae Dominae de Fatima sollemni ritu coronandam censuimus ... Legatum Nostrum deligimus ac renuntiamus, ut in Sanctuario de Fatima inditam Beatae Mariae Imaginem nomine Nostro Nostraque auctoritate aureo diademate exornes'. The coronation itself is recorded in the papal radio message of 13 May 1946, AAS 38 (1946) pp. 264-267, rubric 'NUNTIUS RADIOPHONICUS ... SOLLEMNIA CELEBRANTIBUS AD SANCTUARIUM B. MARIAE V. A FATIMA, AUREA CORONA NOMINE SUMMI PONTIFICIS REDIMITAE' ('por mão do Nosso Cardeal Legado, acabamos de coroar a Imagem taumaturga'). Diocese (Leiria) not named in either text.

sources.act_type: Epistula
sources.rubric_latin: AD EMUM P. D. FRIDERICUM, EPISCOPUM TUSCULANUM, S. R. E. CARDINALEM TEDESCHINI, PATRIARCHALIS BASILICAE VATICANAE ARCHIPRESBYTERUM, SACRI CONSILII PETRIANAE FABRICAE PRAEFECTUM EUNDEMQUE SUMMI PONTIFICIS DATARIUM, LEGATUM DELECTUM AD SACRA SOLLEMNIA IN LUSITANIA AD SIMULACRUM B. VIRGINIS MARIAE DE FATIMA CELEBRANDA.
sources.incipit_latin: Proximo Octobri mense, postquam Congressus Marialis ex omnibus nationibus Ulyssipone in Lusitania habitus fuerit, Anno Sacro, quem ad universum catholicum orbem extendimus
sources.notes: Letter deputing Card. Federico Tedeschini as Legate for the closing solemnities of the Holy Year at Fatima — NOT for a coronation; the crowning is mentioned retrospectively on printed p. 781: « quique eandem sollemni ritu quinque abhinc annos coronandam quoque decrevimus ». 'quinque abhinc annos' from the Datum (24 Sept 1951) gives 1946; the year is not stated outright. `legate` left null because Tedeschini was deputed for the solemnities, not to crown. Diocese not named in the act; Leiria supplied from the place name — verify. The candidate passage is keyed to printed p. 781; the act begins on p. 780, which is cited here.

sources.act_type: Epistula

sources.rubric_latin: AD EMUM P. D. BENEDICTUM EPISCOPUM PRAENESTINUM S. R. E. CARDINALEM ALOISI MASELLA, PATRIARCHALIS BASILICAE LATERANENSIS ARCHIPRESBYTERUM, SACRAE CONGREGATIONIS DE DISCIPLINA SACRAMENTORUM PRO-PRAEFECTUM, QUINQUAGESIMUM SACERDOTII ANNUM IMPLETURUM.

sources.notes: Jubilee letter to Card. Aloisi Masella; the coronation is mentioned only retrospectively on printed p. 467: « Peculiarem quoque benevolentiam Nos tibi significavimus, quum ad coronam simulacro Beatae Mariae Virginis de Fatima apponendam Legatum Nostrum renuntiavimus ». No date given for the crowning. The Datum on p. 468 is OCR-corrupt ('die xviii mensis Maii, anno MDCCCCIII'); the pontifical year ('quarto decimo') fixes it as 1952, so 1952-05-18 — verify. Country inferred from 'de Fatima'.

sources.act_type: Litterae Encyclicae
sources.rubric_latin: AD VENERABILES FRATRES PATRIARCHAS, ARCHIEPISCOPOS, EPISCOPOS ALIOSQUE LOCORUM ORDINARIOS PACEM ET COMMUNIONEM CUM APOSTOLICA SEDE HABENTES: DE REGALI BEATAE MARIAE VIRGINIS DIGNITATE EIUSQUE FESTO INSTITUENDO.
sources.incipit_latin: Ad Caeli Reginam, inde a primis Catholicae Ecclesiae saeculis, supplices preces ac laudis pietatisque cantus christianus populus adhibuit
sources.notes: Encyclical 'Ad caeli Reginam'. The act opens on printed p. 625; the coronation clause falls on p. 627, so aas_page is the act's start page (which here also equals the passage's printed_page). Clause: '...radiophonicum nuntium, quem ad Lusitanorum populum transmisimus, cum prodigialis Mariae Virginis imago, quae Fatimae colitur, aureo diademate redimita fuit' (OCR renders 'colitur' as 'eolito'). Footnote 3 cites A.A.S. 38 (1946) p. 264 — the radio message accompanying the 1946 crowning at Fátima — but this passage states no date, so coronation_date is null. Country inferred from 'ad Lusitanorum populum' + 'Fatimae'; no diocese or sanctuary named.

sources.notes: Basilica Minor elevation act; states in passing 'sive cum Imago Deiparae aureo diademate, Nostro nomine et auctoritate, anno scilicet MCMXLVI, redimiretur' - crowned 1946 in the Pope's name and by his authority; the crowning Legate is not named in the act. Country explicit ('in Lusitanorum finibus'). The act rubric and body begin on printed page 210.

sources.notes: Not an act about a coronation: the attestation is in footnote 6 of the Apostolic Exhortation Signum magnum - 'Nuntius Radiophonicus a Pio XII, die 13 mensis Maii anno 1946, Lusitaniae christifidelibus datus, sollemnia celebrantibus ad templum B. Mariae Fatimensis, aurea corona nomine Summi Pontificis redimitae: A. A. S. 38 (1946) p. 264'. Coronation date taken as the day of those solemnities (13 May 1946) - verify. The exhortation begins on p. 465 (rubric and incipit taken from there); the footnote is on p. 466. Locality 'Fátima' inferred from 'Fatimensis'; country explicit (Lusitania).

Their authority ('autorizza'): Capitolo assenso; officiated by Monsignor Giorgio Francesco Saverio de Marotti, vescovo di Pican; their decree date 22-6-1715. Their annotazioni: ERR - Frate Anselmo: la titola Santa Maria delle Grazie e la colloca a Gorizia. Corona commissionata dalla comunità dei fedeli. Their note: Dipinto del XVI secolo, opera di Palma il Vecchio. Il dipinto fu donato Alla chiesa nel 1544 dal patriarca di Aquileia Marino Grimani. Corone d'oro adorne con perle orientali, diamanti e altre gemme. Le corone furono donate dalla contessa Anna Caterina Scellenburg di Lubiana. Con la firma dei trattati di Parigi nel 1947 la località dove sorge il santuario, Sveta Gora nel comune di Nova Gorica, italiano fino a questa data e più precisamente nel comune di Gorizia, fu assegnato alla ex Jugoslavia.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae (Breve, Ex Secretaria Brevium)
sources.rubric_latin: Ecclesia B. Mariae Virginis Gratiarum in Monte Sancto ad dignitatem Basilicae minoris evehitur.
sources.incipit_latin: In sublimi Beati Petri Cathedra, ad quam licet immerentes evecti sumus, nihil potius habemus, quam sacrarum aedium honor et cultus magis magisque in dies augeatur.
sources.notes: Brief elevating the church to a minor basilica; the coronation is mentioned in passing: 'venerata Deiparae Virginis Imago quae summa religione ibidem colitur iam inde ab anno MDCCXVII ex decreto Capituli Vaticani aureo diademate ornata sit' — i.e. crowned with a golden diadem in 1717 by decree of the Vatican Chapter. The act begins on printed p. 19 (rubric + 'AD PERPETUAM REI MEMORIAM'); the coronation sentence itself falls on p. 20, which is the passage's printed_page. Datum line reads 'die XIX Novembris MCMVI, Pontificatus Nostri anno quarto' = 1906-11-19, one year earlier than the volume year (ASS 40 = 1907); trusted the act. The text places the shrine 'prope Urbem Goritiensem' in 'Austriacae Ditionis' (Austrian Littoral, county of Gorizia, 1907); the modern country is inferred — Sveta Gora / Monte Santo lies today in Slovenia, above Nova Gorica, just across the Italian border — hence confidence lowered to medium. Raw OCR: 'celebérrimas' for 'celeberrimas'. No vernacular title given in the text.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA V., « DE LA CABEZA » VULGO APPELLATA, PRAECIPUA APUD DEUM PATRONA UNA CUM S. EUPHRASIO, EP. ET CONF., UNIVERSAE DIOECESIS GIENNENSIS CONSTITUITUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Studium et cultus Beatae Mariae Virginis, quae « de la Cabeza » Hispanico appellatur sermone, a multo iam tempore animos tenent Illiturgitanorum
sources.notes: Patron declaration that recalls in passing that the Chapter of St Peter's ('Petrianae Basilicae Canonicorum Collegium'), at the request of Bishop Juan Manuel Laguarda Fenollera and in the time of St Pius X, granted 'ut ... Mariale simulacrum aurea corona redimiretur'; no coronation year given. The image, found in 1227 ('anno MCCXXVII') on the mountain, lost its diadem in the Spanish Civil War and a more precious crown was prepared to replace it. Act begins on printed page 383 (passage page-marker is 384). Datum reads 'die XXVII mensis Novembris, anno MDCCCCLVHII' — read as MDCCCCLVIIII = 1959, confirmed by 'Pontificatus Nostri secundo'. Locality Illiturgis = Andújar (identification supplied).

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.rubric_latin: SANCTUARIUM B. M. V. DE ARANZAZU, DIOECESIS VICTORIENSIS, TITULO AC DIGNITATE BASILICAE MINORIS COHONESTATUR.
sources.incipit_latin: In Cantabris montibus, dioecesis Victoriensis intra fines, haud procul ab « Onate », quod est provinciae Guipuzcoae oppidum
sources.notes: Basilica Minor act stating 'eandemque anno MDCCCLXXXVI, clero populoque plaudente, a Victoriensi Episcopo aureo diademate redimitam' - crowned in 1886 by the Bishop of Vitoria; papal authority for that crowning is NOT stated in the passage, hence confidence medium. The same act recalls that Benedict XV himself declared the Virgin of Aranzazu principal patroness of the civil province of Guipuzcoa in 1918. Old stone image of the Virgin with the Infant Jesus. OCR gives 'Ofiate'/'Onate' for Onate (Onati).

Their authority ('autorizza'): B.P.; officiated by Monsignor Antonio Riberi, nunzio apostolico; their decree date 9-5-1966. Their annotazioni: ERR - Bonci: tralascia. Their note: Statua lignea del XIII secolo. Durante la guerra civile spagnola, il 9 agosto 1936, tutte le immagini sacre della città furono distrutte, tranne questa immagine e quella del Padre Nostro Gesù di Nazareth. Purtroppo, pochi giorni dopo, questa fu riportata in città e fatta a pezzi nella piazza del municipio. Solo la testa sopravvisse, che fu recuperata. Dopo la guerra, questa reliquia fu utilizzata per creare una nuova immagine, scolpendo le parti visibili della testa, mentre il resto servì come cornice per vestire l'immagine.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA VIRGO, SUB TITULO « DE URIBARRI », QUAE IN OPPIDO « DURANGO » VICTORIENSIS DIOECESIS VENERATUR, TOTIUS ARCHIPRESBYTERALIS REGIONIS DURANGUENSIS PATRONA COELESTIS DECLARATUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Victoriensis dioecesis intra fines, in oppidi « Durango » nuncupati templo archipresbyterali, Imago quaedam Beatae Mariae Virginis religiosissime colitur sub populari titulo « de Uribarri »
sources.notes: Patron declaration that also grants the coronation: 'ut Imaginem eandem corona Nomine Nostro redimiri decerneremus ... ipsi Venerabili Fratri Episcopo titulo Siandensi, Victoriensis dioecesis Apostolico Administratori, eas partes committimus ut Imaginem ... aureo diademate, nomine atque auctoritate Nostris, sollemniter redimiat'. The executor is the titular Bishop of 'Siandensis', Apostolic Administrator of Vitoria; his personal name is not given in the act, so legate left null. Date of coronation left to him ('die ab eodem statuendo'). Passage printed_page was 221; act begins on printed p. 220. Vernacular title supplied as the Spanish form of the Latin 'de Uribarri' (only the Latin form appears).

XIII, qui inditam imaginem illam per Legatum aureo diademate redimivit' (OCR 'redimi vit'; 'inditam' probably for 'inclitam'). No coronation year and no Legate name given; Leo XIII reigned 1878-1903. Locality 'Lluc' taken from the sanctuary's own epithet; country inferred from 'Balearum Insularum' / dioecesis Maioricensis, not stated in the act. Vernacular form of the title not given beyond « de Lluch ».

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA VIRGO SUB TITULO «DEL CORO», CORONA REDIMITA, CIVITATIS SANCTI SEBASTIANI IN DIOECESI HISPANIAE VICTORIENSI PATRONA DECLARATUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Urbis Sancti Sebastiani intra fines Victoriensis dioecesis in ecclesia paroeciali matrici Sanctae Mariae iam ab annis multis religiosissime asservatur imago Beatae Virginis Mariae vulgo «Virgen del Coro» nuncupata
sources.notes: Combined patron-declaration and coronation grant: the Bishop of Vitoria is charged to crown the image in the Pope's name on a day of his own choosing - 'Venerabili Fratri Victoriensium Episcopo eas partes committimus, ut arbitrio suo eligendo die ... Imaginem Beatae Virginis a Choro praedictam per se ipsum vel per ecclesiasticum virum in dignitate constitutum, et ab eodem deputandum, iuxta ritum formulamque praescripta aureo diademate, servatis servandis, Nostro nomine et auctoritate, post Missarum sollemnia, redimiat'. No legate is named (the ordinary or his delegate). Incipit ('Urbis Sancti Sebastiani') confirmed by the volume index on p. 583.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.legate: Iosephus M. S. R. E. Cardinalis Bueno Monreal, olim Archiepiscopus Hispalensis

sources.incipit_latin: Qui semper castissimam Virginem Mariam, Christi Matrem amabilem, toto corde dileximus, aequo semper animo ea coepta aut inimus aut ineunda probamus

Petition by Abp Carolus Amigo Vallejo of Seville that the crowning be performed, in the Pope's name and authority, by Card. Bueno Monreal, emeritus archbishop. sources.act_type: Epistola
sources.rubric_latin: AD EM.UM P. D. HENRICUM TIT. S. PETRI IN MONTE AUREO S. R. E. PRESB. CARD. REIG Y CASANOVA, ARCHIEPISCOPUM TOLETANUM, DE CONGRESSU EUCHARISTICO EX TOTA HISPANIA.
sources.incipit_latin: Sacras inter aedes, quas catholicae Hispaniae filii, media aetate, excitarunt, principem videtur obtinere locum, cum ob molis amplitudinem
sources.notes: Act I begins on printed p. 52 (the passage page marker is 53). The Pope commends, but does not himself grant, the plan of the Archbishop of Toledo: 'itemque quam vos singulari cultu caelestem Patronam veneramini Virginem a Sacrario, eius effigiem aurea corona redimiendi. Utrumque autem, quod iam in eo es ut perficias, propositum ...'. Prospective, not retrospective, and not the coronation grant itself - classified as retrospective_attestation for want of a better category. No date is given for the crowning (letter dated 4 October 1926, coronation imminent).

sources.act_type: Epistola
sources.legate: Alafridus Ildefonsus S. R. E. Card. Schuster, Archiepiscopus Mediolanensis
sources.rubric_latin: AD EMUM P. D. ALAFRIDUM ILDEFONSUM TIT. SS. SILVESTRI ET MARTINI IN MONTIBUS S. R. E. PRESBYTERUM CARDINALEM SCHUSTER, MEDIOLANENSIUM ARCHIEPISCOPUM: QUEM MITTIT LEGATUM AD SOLEMNIA DECIES SAECULARIA ABBATIAE EINSIDLENSIS.
sources.incipit_latin: Non levi animi delectatione nuper intelleximus de sollemnibus decies saecularibus, quae Einsidlenses monachi in honorem Deiparae « eremitarum Dominae » appellatae summo studio apparare contendunt
sources.notes: Letter deputing Cardinal Schuster as Legate: '... et prodigiosum « eremitarum Dominae » simulacrum, tanta populi veneratione excultum, nomine Nostro Nostraque auctoritate sollemni coronae impositione exornes.' No coronation date stated; the rites were to take place 'proxime' during the 1934 millenary celebrations of the abbey. Country and locality inferred from 'Einsidlensis' (Einsiedeln); the letter names no diocese. OCR 'mtelleximus' repaired to 'intelleximus'.

sources.act_type: Litterae Apostolicae
sources.rubric_latin: TEMPLUM DEO IN HONOREM B. MARIAE V. IMMACULATAE GENEVAE CONSECRATUM HONORIBUS BASILICAE MINORIS INSIGNITUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Nominis Catholici in urbe Geneva revigescentis signum perhibetur esse Templum, quod paulo post sollemniter pronunciatum dogma Immaculati Beatae Mariae Virginis Conceptus exstructum fuit
sources.notes: Clause: « Quod Simulacrum ... anno millesimo nongentesimo trigesimo septimo, Episcoporum, Sacerdotum e prioribus, populi fidelis astante corona, auro diademate, Nostro nomine et auctoritate, fuit redimitum ». The statue is the one Pius IX kept in his apartment and donated to this church. « Nostro nomine et auctoritate » is written by Pius XII of a 1937 event (reigning pope then Pius XI): read as ‘in the name and by the authority of this Apostolic See’.

sources.act_type: Epistula
sources.legate: Manuel Arteaga y Betancourt, Cardinal, Archbishop of San Cristóbal de La Habana
sources.rubric_latin: AD EMUM P. D. EMMANUELEM TIT. SANCTI LAURENTII IN LUCINA S. R. E. PRESB. CARDINALEM ARTEAGA Y BETANCOURT, ARCHIEPISCOPUM SANCTI CHRISTOPHORI DE HABANA, QUEM LEGATUM RENUNTIAT AD IMAGINEM NOSTRAE DOMINAE DE COROMOTO CORONA EXORNANDAM.
sources.incipit_latin: Intra fines dioecesis Barquisimetensis, in Venezuelana Republica sitae, celebre admodum exstat Sanctuarium Beatae Mariae Virginis sub populari titulo « de Coromoto »
sources.notes: The batch passage itself is the volume's chronological index on printed p. 906, which points to the act on p. 722 ('quem Legatum renuntiat ad imaginem Nostrae Dominae de Coromoto corona exornandam 722'); the same act is indexed again at p. 942. aas_page is therefore the act's page (722), not the index page. Rubric, incipit, Datum and details taken from the act text at AAS 44 (1952) 722-723 in the full volume file. Act: '...perinsignem illam imaginem sollemni ritu proximo Septembri mense coronandam per Legatum Nostrum censuimus... ut in Sanctuario de Guanare venerandam imaginem Nostrae Dominae de Coromoto veluti manibus Nostris sacra exornes corona.' coronation_date = September 1952 ('proximo Septembri mense'); the volume also records a papal radio message of 12 Sept 1952 to the Venezuelans celebrating the coronation (p. 739). OCR of the act gives 'Guanare de los Oospes' (= Guanare de los Cospes) and 'Berquisimetensis' alongside 'Barquisimetensis'. Spanish form of the title taken from the radio message text at p. 739 ('Nuestra Señora de Coromoto').

sources.act_type: Nuntius Radiophonicus
sources.rubric_latin: NUNTIUS RADIOPHONICUS CHRISTIFIDELIBUS VENEZUELAE DATUS, SOLLEMNIA IN HONOREM B. MARIAE VIRGINIS DE COROMOTO CELEBRANTIBUS.
sources.incipit_latin: Venerables Hermanos y amados hijos, católicos venezolanos, que en la linda Guanare asistís conmovidos a la solemne coronación de vuestra Excelsa Patrona, Nuestra Señora de Coromoto
sources.notes: Radio message of Pius XII broadcast to Venezuela on the day of the coronation; the footnote reads 'Habita die 12 Septembris mensis a. 1952', which is the delivery date (there is no Datum line) and also the date of the ceremony. The text never uses a word for 'image': it speaks of the devotional title, the people 'colocándole en las sienes una preciosa corona' at 'la solemne coronación de vuestra Excelsa Patrona, Nuestra Señora de Coromoto'. It is not itself the granting act: the papal Legate was deputed by the Litterae at AAS 44 (1952) 722 ('AD IMAGINEM NOSTRAE DOMINAE DE COROMOTO CORONA EXORNANDAM', dated 30 July 1952, Card. Emmanuel Arteaga y Betancourt, Archbishop of Havana), hence retrospective_attestation. The message names the Legate only as 'Nuestro dignísimo Legado', so legate is left null; church_or_sanctuary, diocese_latin and diocese_modern are taken from that companion act at p. 722 (this passage says only 'el gran Santuario Nacional' at Guanare, Venezuela). Rubric OCR reads 'VENEZUELAS' for 'VENEZUELAE'. Incipit is the Spanish salutation, the act having no Latin body.

sources.act_type: Epistola
sources.rubric_latin: Pii PP. X circa coronationem simulacri S. Cordis Iesu.
sources.incipit_latin: Me taedet preces tuas exaudire non posse eo quod S. Rituum Congregatio ultimis hisce diebus incongruum declaravit imaginibus divini Cordis Iesu coronas imponere
sources.notes: NEGATIVE norm, not a grant: Pius X tells Léon Gauthey, Bishop of Nevers, that he cannot grant his petition because the S. Congregation of Rites has just declared it 'incongruum' to impose crowns on images of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, permitting only that a crown be laid at the feet of the statue ('corona ad simulacri pedes deponatur'), which the bishop may do in the Pope's name. Emitted as `norms` per SPEC (general legislation about crowning images) with image fields null, though the letter arises from one concrete case: a simulacrum of the Sacred Heart in the diocese of Nevers (Nivernensis), France, for which no coronation was in fact permitted. Retained because it is the governing rule of the period on crowning Sacred Heart images and explains later refusals. Datum: 'Ex aedibus Vaticanis, die 9 Iulii 1908'. OCR: 'exaudiré' -> 'exaudire'. The letter is indexed at ASS 41, p. 621 ('Epistola Pii X circa coronationem simulacri S. Cordis Iesu ... 621').

sources.act_type: Normae (Sacra Congregatio pro Cultu Divino)
sources.rubric_latin: NORMAE CIRCA PATRONOS CONSTITUENDOS ET IMAGINES B. M. VIRGINIS CORONANDAS — II. De Coronatione Imaginis Beatae Mariae Virginis
sources.incipit_latin: Pluries decursu temporis factum est ut populus christianus, filiali devotione permotus, ardenter peteret et obtineret coronationem alicuius Imaginis B. Mariae Virginis.
sources.notes: General legislation, not a specific image. Issued by the Sacra Congregatio pro Cultu Divino 'de mandato Summi Pontificis' (Paul VI reigning); signed Arturus Card. Tabera, Praefectus, and H. Bugnini, a Secretis. The document heading is on printed page 276; Part I (De Patronis constituendis) runs 276-279 and is dated 19 March 1973; Part II (De Coronatione Imaginis Beatae Mariae Virginis) runs 280-281 and is dated 25 March 1973 — that is the act_date given here. Key provisions: only images of the BVM (painted or sculpted) may be crowned; if Christ is shown with her, both must be crowned; the rite is normally performed by the local Bishop per the Pontificale Romanum; coronation 'nomine et auctoritate Summi Pontificis' by a Pontifical Delegate requires that the image be of real importance to the Church, nation or region, and 'facultas coronandi conceditur per Decretum praedictae Congregationis ac per Litteras Apostolicas in forma Brevis expediendas'. Passages AAS-65-1973-ocr#738 and #739 are back-of-volume index entries pointing to this same act at page 276 and were not emitted separately. Document spans pp. 276-280+.

sources.citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 74r–74v
sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: lettera
sources.rubric_latin: l'istanza dai Soprastanti di cotesta venerata Immagine della Beatiss.ma Vergine detta di S. Luca, di fare alla med.ma il dono della Corona d'oro
sources.notes: Crowns: one ('il dono della Corona d'oro'). Petitioner: the 'Soprastanti di cotesta venerata Immagine' (via a request to the Chapter); the Chapter in turn asks an unnamed prelate ('V.S. Ill.ma') for a relazione. A single (draft) letter from the Chapter asking a prelate to report whether the image ('la tela predetta', a painting on canvas) is ancient and miraculous and has not already received a gold crown; no place, diocese, date or addressee is named. The 'S. Luca' title could suggest a well-known image (e.g. Bologna) but the text does not say so. A margin note at the head of f. 74r ('Instra Donationis Dna Coronat. amiea, fac' foras similiae miraculosi d.', i.e. 'Instrumentum Donationis duarum Coronarum aurearum factae simulacro miraculoso ...') is garbled; it may be the tail of the Cibona note on f. 73v or a heading belonging to this item — no instrument for the S. Luca image is actually present in the range. | Draft/copy of the Chapter's letter to an unnamed prelate asking for a relazione on antiquity and miracles of a painting ('la tela predetta') and whether it has already received a gold crown. No town, church or diocese is given; the famous Madonna di San Luca of Bologna is NOT named in the text and is not asserted here. A garbled margin endorsement at the top of f.74r ('Instra Donationis Dna Coronat. amiea, fac' foras similiae miraculosi d.' = Instrum. Donationis duarum Coronarum aurearum fact. simulacro miraculoso...) may belong to a preceding dossier not visible in this range; hence starts_before_range set true. No concession recorded in these pages.

sources.notes: Crowns: two (a very large one for the Virgin and a medium one for the Child), 109 scudi less 12 grani of gold. The place is unreadable in the OCR ('Chiesa Sant:o daetto di Piera'); it might conceivably be a garbling of 'detta di Penna' but the gold weight (109 scudi) does not match the Penna crowns (65 scudi, 1705 conto). Cover margin: 'Decernitur Visitatio 10 Maii 1694 conceditur 11. Oct: 1694' - assigned to this conto by position, but could refer to the preceding Penna dossier. Emitted per rule 5 as a silversmith's account naming an image not otherwise present.

sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: lettera
sources.rubric_latin: Fiume @ 14. 7bre 1715 — Dev.mo Oblig.mo Serv.e Il Ves.co De Menti
sources.notes: Only the closing lines and the address leaf of a letter to the Vatican Chapter, dated Fiume 14 September 1715 and signed by a bishop whose name the OCR renders 'De Menti'. The image and place it concerns are not visible in this range; the dossier begins in the preceding batch. Emitted only as a range-boundary marker. f.214v (pb 507) carries a bare header 'Corone d'oro' with margin '514' (probably a wrapper sheet), and f.215v.03 (pb 513) carries a stray italic label 'Ancona' with margin '212' — neither yields a record.
